title: SuperGPS: Accurate timing and positioning through an optical-wireless distributed time and frequency reference
funding_scheme: Open technologieprogramma OTP oud STW 2015 STW
summary_nl: The SuperGPS project targets the development of ‘terrestrial GPS’. Like the Global Positioning System, it will provide wireless signals for positioning and clock  synchronization. However, the accuracy and coverage of SuperGPS will go significantly beyond the performance of existing GPS. This will be achieved by a grid of innovative ultra-wideband transmitters, connected and synchronized to an accurate atomic clock through the fiber-optic telecommunications network. Ultimately, this should lead to an ICT infrastructure which does not only provide high-capacity connectivity, but also very accurate positioning and timing. The research will conducted by VU Amsterdam and TU Delft, in collaboration with KPN, VSL, SURFnet, TNO, Fugro Geoservices, and OPNT. A field trial of SuperGPS at the TNO test site (A270 highway) is planned, in order to demonstrate positioning with 10 cm accuracy under real-life conditions.

title: Photronics: Photonic Electronic Integration at the Wafer Scale
funding_scheme: Samenwerkingsprogramma High Tech Systemen en Materialen (HTSM) 2014 STW
summary_nl: We address a breakthrough solution to the problem of integrating photonic and electronic functionality: we fabricate photonic ICs on top of electronic ICs to create a single photronic chip. Photronics: Photonic Electronic Integration at the Wafer Scale 3. We do this using a combination of new technology and full semiconductor wafers from industry production lines. Photronic ICs - single-chip photonic-electronic integrated circuits - will outperform discrete electronic-optical systems in terms of performance, energy-efficiency, physical size and ease of assembly. Critical performance breakthroughs are directly targeted in high-speed data networks and precision metrology, with a number of future potential applications in non-invasive healthcare, safety systems, monitoring and control. If successful, this project will further strengthen the position of the Netherlands in the Photonics landscape and help Europe to leapfrog the US and Asia in photonic-electronic integration.

title: Crossover collaboration for digital innovation
funding_scheme: Creatieve industrie Embedded of Strategisch Embedded Research en Strategisch Onderzoek
summary_nl:
Grand societal challenges, for example related to health, transport, environment, and inequality, require crossover collaboration to develop solutions. Lately, the rise of digital innovations provides promising solutions to respond to these challenges. Such digital innovations require heterogeneous partners from different disciplines and industries to collaborate, for instance independent fashion designers and institutionalized energy corporations, technology and arts, or independent creative actors and large medical organizations. While insight from existing research on collaborations is useful, current crossover collaborations are radically different due to the specific characteristics of digital innovation. This research aims to develop (1) improved understanding of how brokers involve and engage heterogeneous partners (connecting), (2) new approaches of design thinking that are required to create crossover digitized products and services (creating), and (3) insights on how coordination leads to the generation of new business models for crossover digital innovation (coordinating). We use a practice-based, theory development approach that enables revealing the micro-processes of collaboration between heterogeneous partners and interrelating digital technologies. Our research contributes to academic and practical insights on crossover digital innovation initiatives as well as the implications of the emergence of digital innovations for the creative industry and society at large.
The interdisciplinary research combines our expertise on ?design for business?, ?collaborative innovation? and ?knowledge management and information technology?. By means of teaching, publications, regular knowledge sharing workshops among our seven industry partners and a yearly international summerschool, we will guarantee valorization and engage an international community of practitioners and academics.

title: Flexible robotic suit
summary_nl:
Exoskeletons are used to enhance the strength of the wearer as an assistive device as well as for therapy of various groups of patients ranging from stroke survivors, children with cerebral palsy, and spinal cord injured patients. However, these devices are typically bulky, heavy, and uncomfortable and therefore not widely used in daily life.



The aim of this project is to move beyond exoskeletons and develop a light and comfortable flexible robotic suit to improve patients' walking.



Current robotic suits rely on biomimetic solutions with muscle-like actuators pulling on human limbs. This approach is unable to make patients walk again, as the applied pressure peaks and shear stresses at the skin are beyond tolerable levels.

 

My fundamentally different approach is to create a truly biocompatible robotic suit by inverting the interaction: In the inverted Muscle Skeleton (iMS) approach actuators push against the limbs, while stresses and forces are minimised by using a connected network of strings. This network removes the need for a stiff exoskeleton and unloads the body such that the required joint torques for walking can be generated.



The proposed project is divided in six work packages and involves developing and testing algorithms for control, sensing, experiments to iteratively improve design and control and evaluation of six SCI patients and six stroke survivors. The project is carried out by a team of three Ph.D. students, two post docs, and two technicians under my direct guidance. Clinicians, therapists, and researchers will be involved in the user-centred design process and clinical studies.



Clinicians, therapists, and researchers of the rehabilitation centres the Roessingh in Enschede and the Sint Maartens Clinic in Nijmegen, and the Free University Medical Centre in Amsterdam, will be involved in the user centred design process and clinical studies. In addition, we will intensively collaborate and exchange researchers and students with Conor Walsh from the Wyss Institute for Biologically Inspired Engineering of Harvard University, who has much experiences in development and testing of soft exosuits, and with Hartmut Geyer from the Robotic Institute of Carnegie Mellon University who is the expert in neuromuscular robotic control.



Based on a promising and novel approach and my proven track record in the field of development of wearable exoskeleton technology, this project has the potential to develop a system that can improve the quality of walking and life of millions, reduce treatment costs, and target a multi-million market. Involvement of user groups and representatives from industry facilitate adequate take-up by users and industry.

title: Alle kinderen zijn gelijk maar sommige zijn meer gelijk dan anderen. Het verbeteren van Engels leren op school
funding_scheme: Programmaraad voor Fundamenteel Onderzoek - samenhangende onderzoeksprojecten 2014 NRO
summary_nl: Uitstekende vaardigheden in het Engels worden van groot belang geacht voor maatschappelijk succes. Ondanks dat Engels een verplicht vak is en er recent striktere exameneisen zijn gekomen is de optimale afstemming van Engels onderwijs op de individuele verschillen tussen leerlingen vooralsnog onduidelijk. Factoren die de afstemming tussen Engels onderwijs in basis en voortgezet onderwijs kunnen verbeteren dienen te worden bepaald. Dit project heeft twee doelen: 1). Het opsporen van voorspellers voor succesvol Engels leren in de laatste twee jaar van het basisonderwijs en tijdens de eerste twee jaar van het voortgezet onderwijs 2). Het ontwikkelen van onderwijsmethoden voor optimaal Engels leren door individuele leerlingen. Deze onderzoeksdoelen worden in twee deelprojecten bestudeerd. Het eerste deelproject richt zich op voorspellers van Engelse taalvaardigheid binnen een longitudinaal onderzoek en op het onderwijzen van de Engelse lees- en schrijfvaardigheid. Deelproject 2 richt zich op onderwijsmethoden voor het verbeteren van mondelinge taalvaardigheid in het Engels. (150 woorden)

title: Nutritional programming of brain development and function: can it protect against early-life stress induced (accelerated) cognitive decline?
funding_scheme: Food, Cognition and Behaviour - Groot project 2014 NIHC
summary_nl: In de periode vlak na de geboorte blootstelling aan stress kan de bouw en functie van ons brein levenslang  beïnvloeden en wordt geassocieerd met verminderde cognitie op latere leeftijd. Juist tijdens deze fase zijn voedingsstoffen noodzakelijk voor de brein. In dit project bestuderen we het belang van voeding voor programmering van hersenfunctie door stress en of voeding bescherming kan bieden tegen de gevolgen van stress. We onderzoeken, in zowel (pre)klinische setting, of blootstelling aan stress tijdens de postnatale ontwikkeling de samenstelling van moedermelk beïnvloedt en of vroege voedings-interventie, de blijvende gevolgen van stress op het brein kan verminderen of voorkomen.
summary_en: During the postnatal phase exposure to stress can persistently impact brain structure and function and has been associated with later life cognitive decline.  During this sensitive developmental period, nutrients are essential for the brain. In this project we study the role of nutrition on the programming of the brain by early-stress and if nutrition early in life can protect against the lasting impacts thereof. We investigate in a (pre)clinical setting if stress alters breastmilk composition  and if and how nutritional intervention protect agains the detrimental effects of early-life stress.

title: "Numbering Life. Metrics and Measures in Digital Media"
summary_nl: The project "Numbering Life. Metrics and Measures in Digital Media" responds to the growing quantification of social and cultural life in digital culture. It explores the making, circulation and evaluation of numbers in social media platforms, such as Like, friend or share counts, numbers of interactions, algorithmic influence ranks or popularity metrics. In the context of contemporary audit cultures platforms constantly transform user activities into different numerical forms which allow users to evaluate themselves or be evaluated and valorised by third-party organisations and researchers. The distinctive claim put forward by this project is to approach these numbers not as representative, external descriptors, but as fabricated enumerated entities, which inform what they seek to measure and come with an (after)life. It addresses numbers as part of wider number ecologies and shows how third-party platforms, commercial and academic research de- and recontextualise these numbers, making users accountable for their social media activities alongside multiple value axis. Attending to the role of users, platforms and third-parties involved, the project investigates how numbers in digital media allow to create specific relations between social and economic value. Methodologically, the project draws on software analysis, digital methods and business ethnography to conduct six empirical case studies on the history and making of numbers, the multiplicity of meaning of numbered activities, the use of numbers for reputation and risk assessment in reputation algorithms, the numbering practices of wearable devices for self-quantification and the use of platform metrics in commercial and academic research to study mediated social life. The project offers the first conceptual and methodological framework for the study of numbers in digital media and brings together emergent debates in number theory, software and platform studies, as well as digital humanities, offering an inventive contribution to public debates on number/data driven life.

title: Levels of social inference: Investigating the origin of human uniqueness
summary_nl:
Humans are a uniquely social species. Our lives are dominated by interactions with others, thinking about others, and talking to others about others. How did we become this social? In this project we investigate the hypothesis that we did not obtain completely new social skills, but rather that we are capable of processing the social information we get from others at a deeper level than other species do. Similarly, we hypothesize that this ability is supported not by completely new brain regions, but by a change in the way information is processed in the brain. We will test this hypothesis by constructing a formal computational model of the cognitive architecture that underlies human social information processing. This model will be a hierarchical Bayesian model that processes incoming social information, for instance about the movements make by another person in a competitive game, first at a superficial level processing the movement patterns, and then at a deeper level processing the intentions behind the movements.
Having developed and validated the model we will then test whether this type of architecture is present in our brains. We will do this by using a comparative method. First, we will compare the organization of the brain of humans to that of less social non-human primates to see whether there are differences in the connections between brain areas processing social information. Second, we will compare the organization of the brains of different human individuals to investigate if the connections that are unique to humans indeed mediate social cognition. Finally, we will compare the working of the brain in the same individuals before and after ?virtual lesions? to areas of the brain processing social information to see if indeed social information processing occurs in the hierarchical fashion hypothesized in our model.

title: Videogebruik van eigen stagelessen bij het leren van rekenen-wiskundedidactiek door pabostudenten
summary_nl: Hoewel pabostudenten veel theoretische kennis leren, is het voor reken-wiskundeopleiders niet altijd duidelijk of en hoe studenten aangeleerde theorie in de praktijk toepassen. In dit onderzoek wordt nagegaan wat de meerwaarde is van het opnemen en bewerken van eigen lessen op video uit de stage en de bespreking en reflectie daarop in de PABO. Eerst wordt de bestaande situatie rond videogebruik op de opleiding beschreven, evenals de self-efficacy van leraren-in-opleiding, hun vakdidactische kennis en hun vakdidactisch handelen. Vervolgens wordt tijdens een quasi-experiment met twee experimentele condities en een controlegroep kennis verworven over de meerwaarde van de inzet van video.

title: Het gebruik van een praktisch didactisch model door beginnend docenten voor het leren ontwerpen van lessen
summary_nl: In dit onderzoek wordt gekeken of het didactisch bouwstenen model, beginnend docenten kan ondersteunen bij het ontwerpen van lessen. Hierbij wordt ingegaan op de verschillende componenten van een les zoals doelen, inhoud, werkvormen, onderwijsleerproces en controle. Vernieuwend is dat voor alle componenten keuzemogelijkheden zijn uitgewerkt met het karakter van bouwstenen.

title: Self-interacting asymmetric dark matter
summary_nl: De meeste materie in ons heelal bestaat uit een nog onbekend soort deeltjes die niet met licht interageren, bekend als donkere materie. De zwaartekracht van donkere materie is grotendeels verantwoordelijk voor de vorming van de galactische structuren zoals wij die waarnemen. Gedetailleerde waarnemingen van de galactische structuur kunnen mogelijk informatie onthullen over de eigenschappen van donkere materie, met name de manier waarop deze met zichzelf en met andere deeltjes interageert. De juiste interpretatie van dergelijke waarnemingen vereist systematisch en zorgvuldig onderzoek van deeltjesfysische modellen van donkere materie, en de kosmologie en astrofysica die zij impliceren.
summary_en: Most of the matter in our universe is made of some yet unknown type of particles that do not interact with light, known as dark matter. The gravitational pull of dark matter is largely responsible for the formation of the galactic structures as we observe them. Detailed observations of the galactic structure can potentially reveal information about the properties of dark matter, in particular the way it interacts with itself and with other particles. The correct interpretation of such observations necessitates the systematic and careful investigation of particle physics models of dark matter, and the cosmology and astrophysics they imply.

title: Building a sustainable greenhouse gas sink in Dutch delta soils.
summary_nl:
We ontwikkelden een nieuw model (PVN) om de CO2-opname en CH4-emissie van wetland-natuurontwikkeling te simuleren. In dit model is een vegetatiesuccessiemodel (NUCOM) en een bodemkoolstofmodel (Peatland-VU) gecombineerd. Het model maakt gebruik van grondwaterstandsgegevens uit grondwatermodellen van Deltares.

Het model is getest op CO2/CH4-emissiegegevens van twee natuurontwikkelingsgebieden en reproduceert een realistische vegetatieopvolging en CO2/CH4-uitwisseling met de atmosfeer. Publicatie wordt medio 2022 verwacht. Verdere modelontwikkeling, verbetering en toepassing (koolstofopslag, schaalvergroting, natte landbouw) vindt plaats in het kader van NOBV (Nationaal Onderzoeksprogramma Broeikasgasemissie Veenland).
summary_en:
We developed a new model (PVN) to simulate the CO2 uptake and CH4 emission from wetland nature development. In this model a vegetation succession model (NUCOM) and a soil carbon model (Peatland-VU) have been combined. It uses groundwater table data input from groundwater models of Deltares.

The model has been tested on CO2/CH4 emission data from two nature development areas and reproduces a realistic vegetation succession and CO2/CH4 exchange. Publication is expected medio 2022. Further model development, improvement and application (carbon storage, larger spatial scale, paludiculture) will occur within the framework of NOBV (national peatland greenhouse gas research programme).

title: Sexuality, religion and secularism. Cultural encounters in the African diaspora in the Netherlands
funding_scheme: Vrije competitie Vrije competitie GW VC 2014 GW
summary_nl:
In the Netherlands, as in Europe generally, debates on migration often problematize the role of religion and "tradition", particularly in relation to gender and sexuality. Religion and tradition are seen as sources of taboos and unsafe practices. In recent years, concerns have emerged about the role of religious leaders in the African Diaspora, for example vis-a-vis promoting anti-gay views and the belief that homosexuality and HIV/AIDS can be miraculously healed.



In addressing these concerns, Dutch public health organizations often depart from the assumption that religion and tradition will be privatized or dwindle in the process of integration. In contrast, recent research shows that in the African Diaspora, religion often plays a major role in the (self) fashioning of individuals. Remarkably, the ways in which religion contributes to the ways African migrants conceptualize and address sexual well-being has only been studied minimally.

 

Through the expertise of the applicants, the project brings together the latest conceptual developments and theoretical debates within the study of religion and the anthropology of sexuality and gender. This has resulted in a multilevel intersectional research design uniquely suited to the pluralistic context of the research. The interactions between Dutch and African understandings of sexual well-being are brought into view at different levels and from different perspectives.

 

The following perspectives, corresponding to the sub-projects are distinguished: I) Dutch organizations with a public health approach to sexuality, II) African religious actors and III) African migrants themselves. Each of the sub-projects and the synthesizing study will develop a fresh contribution to academic debates on sexual nationalisms and the ways religion and secularity are (re)shaped through cultural encounters in a post-colonial Europe. Finally, knowledge valorisation activities will ensure that the project will contribute to the work of public health professionals and religious leaders in a pluralistic setting.

title: We learn from our mistakes - or do we? Towards more efficient use of talking and listening experience in a second language.
summary_nl:
Foutje? Bedankt!

Wie een tweede taal leert, krijgt te maken met ‘vreemde’, nieuwe klanken. De kans op fouten is groot, maar hoe leer je van die fouten als je ze zelf niet opmerkt? Mirjam Broersma ging op zoek naar de beste manier om te leren van je fouten, en ontdekte dat misverstanden tijdens gesprekken helpen. Wanneer tweede-taalleerders verkeerd worden verstaan verbeteren ze hierdoor hun uitspraak, en wanneer tweede-taalleerders de ander verkeerd verstaan verbeteren ze hun waarneming. Voorwaarde is wel dat de ander duidelijk aangeeft wat ze bedoelden (“ik bedoelde niet EEND maar EIND”), of welk woord ze verkeerd verstonden.
summary_en: When you learn a second language, you have to deal with 'strange', new sounds. Mistakes are easily made, but how do you learn from those mistakes if you don't notice them yourself? Mirjam Broersma went looking for the best way to learn from your mistakes, and discovered that misunderstandings during conversations help. When second language learners are misunderstood, they improve their pronunciation, and when second language learners misunderstand the other person, they improve their perception. But only if the other person clearly indicates what they meant (“I didn't mean SIT but SET”), or exactly which word they misunderstood.

title:
Differentiation in teaching from the international perspective: cross-country comparison, development over time, and importance for students’ academic

engagement
funding_scheme: NRO OPRO Differentiatie in het Onderwijs 2014 NRO
summary_nl:
Dit onderzoeksproject dat in meerdere landen is uitgevoerd geeft antwoord op de volgende onderzoeksvragen:

1.	Zijn de Nederlandse maten voor gedifferentieerde instructie betrouwbaar en valide in andere landen?  

2.	Hoe vergelijken VO docenten in Nederland m.b.t. gedifferentieerde instructie in vergelijking met collega's in andere landen?

3.	Welke persoonlijke en contextuele factoren verklaren verschillen in gedifferentieerde instructie tussen landen?

4.	Hoe ontwikkelen gedifferentieerde instructie vaardigheden zich in de tijd tussen landen? 

5.	Welke persoonlijke en contextuele factoren verklaren verschillen en groei in gedifferentieerde instructie tussen landen? 

6.	Wat is de impact van (veranderingen in) gedifferentieerde op de academische betrokkenheid van leerlingen?
summary_en:
The main focus of this international project was answer to the following questions: 

1. How comparable are responses gathered with instruments (observation and student questionnaire), developed in the Dutch context, for measuring Differentiated Instruction in diverse international contexts (Step 1, Research Question 1). 

2. How does the quality of Differentiated Instruction compare across diverse international contexts (Step 2, Research Questions 2 and 3).

3. Do Differentiated Instruction practices change over time, and are there (longitudinal) links between Differentiated Instruction and academic engagement across diverse international contexts (Step 3, Research question 4 - 6)

title: Manipulating the interplay between superconductivity and chiral magnetism at the single atom level
summary_nl: Some of the most pressing questions in condensed matter physics today involve how exchange interactions behave at the atomic scale.  Most notably, magnets which exhibit magnetization with a special sense of rotation, or chirality, and how they interface superconductors are receiving special attention. Traditionally, mixing magnets and superconductors is like mixing oil and water, and yet many proposals in quantum information as well as theories of unconventional superconductivity, are based on the odd mixture of these two phenomena.  At the forefront are so-called Majorana Fermions, which can be realized with a peculiar combination of exchange fields, for example generated by chiral magnets, and superconductors.  Insight into such concepts necessitates experiments which can probe exchange interactions, for example generated by atomic magnets, and how they interact with the electronic degrees of freedom of the substrate.  Such highly desired experiments were not possible until recently, as they must combine high spatial, energy, and magnetic resolution.  The objective of this proposal is to understand how magnetism and superconductivity interact by probing exchange interactions in superconductors, at the single atom level, to gain insight into phenomena like Majoranas and novel proximity effects between superconductors and magnets. The innovative perspectives here are now possible due to the so-called ?spin workbench,? a technique I have developed which combines atomic spin detection and bottom-up fabrication based on scanning tunneling microscopy. This approach will allow us, for the first time, to fabricate in-situ nano-magnets with tailored magnetic properties on superconducting surfaces, to: (i) probe magnetic/superconducting proximity effects driven by chiral magnets, and possible spin-triplet pairing near interfaces, with atomic resolution, and (ii) how indirect exchange interactions generated by single magnetic atoms behave in superconductors, as compared to metals, and if such information can be used to tailor chiral magnets and Majoranas.

title: Grip op dyslexie in het voortgezet onderwijs
summary_nl:
De druk in het onderwijs om leerlingen met dyslexie te ondersteunen is hoog. Op het voortgezet onderwijs wordt

een aanzienlijke hoeveelheid leerlingen gediagnosticeerd. De vraag is hoe deze leerlingen verschillen van degenen

wier ernstige lees/spellingsproblemen al op het basisonderwijs worden gesignaleerd (vraag 1). Daarnaast is de

vraag welke ondersteuning welke leerlingen met dyslexie in het VO kan helpen, auditieve ondersteuning van het

lezen of ondersteuning van tekstaanpak (vraag 2). Dit wordt onderzocht door een profielanalyse en een

inventarisatie van leerlingervaringen (vraag 1), alsmede de effectiviteit van twee ondersteuningsprogramma's

(vraag 2). De bevindingen kunnen concreet handvatten bieden voor het voortgezet onderwijs.

title: Pedagogisch handelen van leraren basisonderwijs onder druk?
summary_nl: Vanwege recente ontwikkelingen in het basisonderwijs die gericht zijn op het versterken van leeropbrengsten en didactiek van leraren, lijkt het pedagogisch handelen onder druk te staan. Deze veronderstelling wordt in dit onderzoek allereerst onderzocht met behulp van een survey-onderzoek naar percepties en leerbehoeften van leraren. Vervolgens wordt het huidige vaardigheidsniveau van en de relatie tussen het pedagogisch en didactisch handelen onderzocht met behulp van lesobservaties (ICALT). Op basis van deze resultaten worden leraren geselecteerd voor een werkplekgerelateerde interventie om het niveau van pedagogisch handelen te versterken. Hiervan worden de effecten onderzocht met behulp van lesobservaties (ICALT) en vragenlijsten.

title: Consumptie van vruchtensappen en de relatie met chronische ziekten, in vergelijking met fruit en frisdrank, bij volwassenen en kinderen
summary_nl: Er is sterk wetenschappelijk bewijs dat fruitconsumptie een beschermend effect heeft op het ontstaan van chronische ziekten, maar er is nog onvoldoende bewijs of ditzelfde geldt voor vruchtensappen. Vruchtensappen bevatten namelijk minder vezels en vitamine C. Er zijn zelfs aanwijzingen dat een hoge consumptie van vruchtensappen ongunstige gezondheidseffecten heeft. In dit promotieonderzoek worden daarom de associaties tussen consumptie van vruchtensappen en respectievelijk astma, cardiometabool risico, hart- en vaatziekten en diabetes mellitus type 2 onderzocht bij kinderen en volwassenen. Hiervoor worden data gebruikt afkomstig van drie grote Nederlandse cohortstudies die geanalyseerd worden met behulp van verschillende statistische analyses.

title: Evaluatie van twee beleidsinterventies in het mbo: inwerkingtreding wet 'Doelmatige Leerwegen' en herziening kwalificatiestructuur
funding_scheme: Evaluatie van twee beleidsinterventies in het mbo 2014 NRO
summary_nl:
Momenteel zijn twee belangrijke beleidsinterventies in het middelbaar beroepsonderwijs (mbo) aan de orde, namelijk de inwerkingtreding van de wet ?Doelmatige Leerwegen? en de herziening van de kwalificatiestructuur. In een meerjarig evaluatieprogramma wordt in beeld gebracht hoe de voortgang van de implementatie van de interventies verloopt, in welke mate de beoogde effecten optreden, welke onbedoelde effecten optreden en hoe de effecten verklaard kunnen worden. In het onderzoeksvoorstel staan de volgende onderzoeksvragen centraal:
- Hoe worden specifieke beleidsmaatregelen - met de betrokkenheid van management, docenten, studenten en bedrijfsleven - ingevoerd in het mbo?
- Leiden de ingevoerde maatregelen daadwerkelijk tot de beoogde effecten?
- Welke andere (onbedoelde) effecten hebben de maatregelen en hoe kunnen de (bedoelde en onbedoelde) effecten worden verklaard?
In het onderzoek worden, ter beantwoording van deze vragen, drie deelprojecten onderscheiden, namelijk de Implementatiemonitor, de Effectevaluatie en de Verklarende evaluatie. De Implementatiemonitor volgt de implementatie van de beleidsmaatregelen op de verschillende niveaus aan de hand van kwantitatieve en kwalitatieve data. De Effectevaluatie kijkt vooral naar de kwantitatieve effecten van het beleid (implementatie-effecten en outcome) aan de hand van beschikbare, bestaande databestanden en eigen dataverzameling. In de Verklarende evaluatie wordt naar een verklaring gezocht voor optredende (gewenste en ongewenste) effecten.
Gekozen is voor een mixed-methods benadering met een combinatie van verschillende kwantitatieve en kwalitatieve methoden, waaronder bestandsanalyse op bestaande steekproef- en registerbestanden, aanvullende dataverzameling bij alle mbo-instellingen en verdiepende casestudies bij een vaste groep mbo-instellingen.
Het onderzoek omvat een uitgebreid programma voor kennisdeling op wetenschappelijk, beleidsmatig en praktijkniveau.

title: Oorlog in de klas. Een geschiedenis van het Nederlandse middelbaar onderwijs en zijn functioneren onder nationaalsocialistische druk tijdens de Duitse bezetting.
summary_nl: De Duitse machthebbers eisten tijdens de bezetting dat de Nederlandse samenleving zich zou voegen naar de nationaalsocialistische "Nieuwe Orde". Ze wilden het middelbaar onderwijs gebruiken om een nieuwe generatie in nationaalsocialistische geest op te voeden. Het gevolg was dat het onderwijsbestel werd geconfronteerd met een reeks van repressieve maatregelen. Leerlingen, docenten, schoolbesturen en vakorganisaties werden voor de keuze gesteld hier wel of niet in mee te gaan, met alle gevolgen van dien. Dit onderzoek brengt de talrijke momenten van worsteling aan het licht en analyseert de botsing tussen de waardesystemen van de diverse Nederlandse samenleving en de totalitaire Führerstaat.

title: De proef op het leven. Over het proza van Johan de Meester en verwante realistische schrijvers en de plaats van dit proza in de literatuur van na 1890.
summary_nl: Leerlingen zullen bij de term 'moderne letterkunde' niet denken aan literatuur uit de periode van 1880 tot 1930. Toch is deze literatuur, specifiek het proza van Johan de Meester, modern in vele opzichten. De grote afstand in tijd en wereldbeeld heeft een groot voordeel: de vervreemding werkt prikkelend en nodigt uit tot verdieping. Tegelijkertijd is er herkenning: het proza is verrassend goed leesbaar en bevat herkenbare thema's zoals sociale en maatschappelijke uitsluiting, (onconventionele) liefdesrelaties, vooroordelen en schijnheiligheid. Hierdoor is deze literatuur bij uitstek een geschikt middel om vanuit historisch perspectief te reflecteren op de maatschappij van nu.

title: Tegen grenzen leren aanlopen
summary_nl: Hoogbegaafde leerlingen zijn vaak onderpresteerders. Zwak ontwikkelde metacognitieve vaardigheden en weerzin tegen automatiserende taken zijn een mogelijke oorzaak hiervan. Metacognitieve vaardigheden kunnen worden verworven mits leerlingen complexe taken krijgen aangeboden met gerichte aandacht voor het leerproces. Latijnse teksten vertalen is zo?n complexe taak, die geschikt is om de metacognitie aan te spreken. Hiervoor moet dan wel een andere vertaaldidactiek toegepast worden dan gebruikelijk. In de didactiek die ik voorstel staat het bevorderen van de metacognitie centraal, waardoor automatiseren een intrinsieke noodzaak wordt en de weerstand daartegen afneemt. Met dit onderzoek verwacht ik het effect van deze didactiek vast te stellen.

title: Waardengeladen kritisch denken bevorderen door filosofische gesprekken in de filosofieles
summary_nl: Kritisch denken is een belangrijke 21e-eeuwse vaardigheid. In dit onderzoek wordt een filosofische gespreksvorm ontwikkeld en geëvalueerd die transferabel, waardengeladen kritisch denken bevordert. Via casestudies wordt nagegaan in hoeverre en hoe lessen filosofie hier nu al op zijn gericht. In een ontwerponderzoek wordt een nieuwe gespreksvorm ontwikkeld met transfer- en waardenbevorderende kenmerken. In een quasi-experimentele studie waaraan dertig leraren filosofie met een vierde klas deelnemen, wordt het effect van deze gespreksvorm op het waardengebonden kritisch denken van leerlingen onderzocht. Daarbij wordt gebruik gemaakt van een redeneervaardighedentest en een essayopdracht m.b.t. waardengeladen kritisch denken over een filosofisch en een biologisch onderwerp.

title: Het effect van creatief schrijven op het schrijfproces en de tekstkwaliteit
summary_nl: Er is opnieuw aandacht voor creativiteit: het is een ?21st century skill?.  Het stimuleren van creativiteit bij Nederlands kan zowel de schrijfvaardigheid verbeteren als het creatieve denken. Onderzocht wordt of onderwijs in creatief schrijven de schrijfvaardigheid van leerlingen (4-havo/vwo) verbetert, in termen van tekstkwaliteit en schrijfstrategieën. In experiment één wordt het effect van creatief schrijven vergeleken met zakelijk schrijven. Experiment twee test of toevoeging van een transfercomponent aan de cursus creatief schrijven de transfer naar zakelijk schrijven vergroot.

title: Stimuleren van een Actieve Leefstijl van VMBO leerlingen
summary_nl: Overgewicht bij jongeren is een van de grootste gezondheidkundige uitdagingen. Vooral bij VMBO jongeren is overgewicht een probleem. Bij deze groep gaat dat samen met een verminderde lichamelijke fitheid. Dit vergroot de kans op chronische ziekten op latere leeftijd. Beweeginterventies werkzaam voor vwo en havo scholieren blijken voor VMBO'ers ineffectief. Vermoedelijk sluiten deze interventies niet goed aan op de belevingswereld van VMBO?ers. In dit onderzoek worden een mix van traditioneel ontworpen interventies vergeleken met die waarbij de interventiemix afgestemd is op de vmbo leerling zėlf zodat ze op basis van hun eigen motivatie een gezonder (beweeg)gedrag gaan vertonen.

title: Development of urea sorbents for dialysate regeneration
summary_nl:
Patients with end stage kidney disease (ESKD) undergo dialysis to replace kidney function. Although life-saving, conventional dialysis has major shortcomings. The treatment is time-consuming and removal of waste molecules and excess water is inadequate, contributing significantly to poor life quality, severe health problems and high mortality (15‐20% per year). Treatment costs are very high.
Goal of this project is to develop an efficient urea sorbent for a miniature artificial kidney device. The project is part of a large research effort, initiated in 2009 by several academic centers, the Dutch Kidney Foundation (DKF) and private partners, to develop a miniature dialysis device. The concept is based on continuous regeneration of a small amount of dialysis fluid. A user-friendly wearable or portable dialysis device, providing dialysis outside the hospital, will represent a huge leap forward for dialysis patients and will significantly increase their quality of life. The device will allow continuous or more frequent dialysis which will improve removal of waste solutes and excess fluid, and hence patient health. The miniaturized design, independent of a fixed water supply, offers freedom and autonomy to the patient. Major cost reduction will be achieved (estimates by DKF yield a 40% reduction).
In recent years, a laptop-sized prototype dialysis device has been constructed, that adequately removes most organic waste solutes and waste ions. However, thus far we have no adequate strategy for removal of urea, which is one of the main obstacles for successful realization of a miniature artificial kidney device. Urea is the waste solute with the highest daily production (as primary waste product of nitrogen metabolism) and exerts toxic effects at high plasma concentrations. However, urea is difficult to bind and has low reactivity. Since effective urea removal is crucial for successful dialysate regeneration, the aim of this proposal is to develop sorbents with high binding capacity for urea, suitable for application in a miniature artificial kidney device. Two complementary approaches will be explored:
1. Development of macromolecular polycarbonyl compounds with high urea binding capacity.
High urea binding capacity and fast binding kinetics will be obtained by the use of ?self-supporting? urea-binding structures (minimal ?dead weight?) with a high density of urea-reactive carbonyl groups, sophisticated arrangement of these groups and high swelling capacity (hydrophilicity) of the sorbent. 
2. Development of urea imprinted polymers with high urea binding capacity.
This approach relies on the use of functional monomers that are bound to urea and are subsequently fixed in a polymer network, followed by removal of the template urea molecules. The resulting imprinted cavities are complementary to the shape of urea and are surrounded by well-positioned functional groups that can interact with the urea molecules. 
The synthesized urea sorbents will be fully characterized in vitro and tested for biocompatibility, followed by incorporation in a miniature dialysis device for in vitro- and in vivo testing (on goats). At the end of the project we expect to have a biocompatible urea sorbent with proven in vivo-efficacy.
summary_en: Goal of the project is to develop an efficient urea sorbent, a key element for the wearable artificial kidney device. A miniature dialysis device will represent a major leap forward for dialysis patients. Continuous or more frequent and longer treatment will significantly improve removal of waste molecules and excess fluid, while the miniaturized design, independent of a fixed water supply, offers more freedom to the patient, resulting in a much higher quality of life. The concept is based on continuous regeneration of a small amount of dialysate. In recent years we have constructed a prototype that adequately removes most organic waste solutes and waste ions. However, thus far we have no adequate strategy for removal of urea, the primary waste product of nitrogen metabolism. Since effective urea removal is crucial for successful filtrate regeneration, the aim of this proposal is to develop polymeric sorbents with high binding capacity for urea by using advanced chemical techniques.

title: Het effect van serious gaming op rekenkundig handelen in medicatieveiligheid
summary_nl: Deze studie richt zich op het professionaliseren van verpleegkundigen in medicatieveiligheid door middel van een serious game. De didactiek in het ontwerp van de serious game is gericht op authentieke  en betekenisvolle leerervaringen. De feedback ('cues') en game kenmerken in het scenario dragen bij aan het rekenkundig handelen in medicatieveiligheid en het bewust zijn van de (aanstaande) professional op dit handelen. Het scenario wordt aangeboden aan 90 eerstejaars studenten van drie hogescholen verpleegkunde en aan 180 professionals in twee ziekenhuizen. De resultaten uit het onderzoek worden gebruikt als input voor een nieuw ontwerpcurriculum

title: Reconfigurable meta-instruments for sensing and inspection
funding_scheme: Samenwerkingsprogramma High Tech Systemen en Materialen (HTSM) 2015 STW
summary_nl: This project aims to realize a novel type of instrumentation for high-throughput, sensitive, nanoscale-resolution sensing and inspection/imaging. The prospect of this technology is the rapid detection of nanoscale defects and contaminants on masks, wafers or any large substrate. Our concept relies on subwavelength optical field localization enabled by photonic metamaterials. In particular, we will develop metamaterials in which the optical field is reconfigurable in a fast and flexible fashion, either through nanomechanical actuation or controlling illumination conditions. Nano-optomechanical or optical reconfiguration will thus enable agile sensors and imaging systems, in which many nanoscale optical detection volumes can be scanned over a large surface and detected in a parallel fashion. We will investigate how the complex coherent interactions of the nanoscale resonators that form the metamaterial constituents, together with compressive sensing concepts, can enhance the flexibility and throughput of the technique. It simultaneously addresses the two main challenges of optical nanoscopy: speed and efficiency. We will take the first steps towards integrating these disruptive concepts in a near-field imaging instrument. Combining different expertise, ranging from metamaterials/nano-optomechanics/plasmonics (AMOLF) and antennas/metamaterials (TU/e) to optomechanics/mechatronics (TU Delft), we address the stringent photonic, mechanical, and instrumentational constraints. In particular, high resolution, high sensitivity, and large measurement bandwidth will be ensured through multi-scale optical and mechanical design of the full meta-instrument.

title: CHEMOSENSE: data-driven approaches for food products with superior sensorial properties
funding_scheme: Fonds Nieuwe Chemische Innovaties - Technology Area (TA) 2015 CW
summary_nl: Ons voedsel is chemisch complex en deze complexiteit is bijzonder hoog voor mengsels zoals soepen en sauzen. Binnen Chemosense zijn nieuwe analytische methodes ontwikkeld om de chemische compositie van soepen en sauzen te bepalen. Daarna, zijn smaakpanels gebruikt om de zelfde producten in detail te beoordelen op geur en smaak. Nieuwe statistische benaderingen zijn ontwikkeld om de analytische data te koppelen aan die van de smaakpanels. Zodoende werd het mogelijk om te voorspellen welke stofjes in de soepen bepalend kunnen zijn voor specifieke geur/smaak attributen.
summary_en: The food we eat is chemically complex. This complexity is especially prevalent in processed soups and sauces. Within Chemosense we developed new analytical approaches to determine the chemical composition of food. We evaluated how novel analytical approaches can be applied to soups and soy sauce. Once these were developed, human sensory panels evaluated the sensory profiles of soup preparations with highly contrasting flavour and aroma profiles. We then developed novel statistical approaches to allow us to couple chemical data and sensory data and make predictions on which chemical ingredients might be causal to certain taste and aroma attributes.

title: Coherent Fourier Scatterometry for fast and sensitive detection of subwavelength structures and particles
funding_scheme: Samenwerkingsprogramma High Tech Systemen en Materialen (HTSM) 2015 STW
summary_nl: We investigate and optimize new techniques to detect  nanostructures and nano-particles in semiconductor and plastic-based fabrication technologies. The technique should be fast, operate in-line and applicable to large areas. Since the structures are too small to be imaged, we will implement scatterometry. Scatterometry has important advantages, namely that it operates in the far field, is non-destructive and requires only relatively low light power levels. However, the measured scattered intensities first have to be processed to be able to retrieve the relevant parameters of the nano-structures. Because the structures are far sub-wavelength, this leads to a severely inverse problem which must be regularized.  To achieve ultimate resolution in scatterometry, the full complex polarization scattering matrix should be measured and processed. In the case of a periodic sample, this requires illumination by a high NA focused spot, in contrast with spatially incoherent illumination that is used in classical scatterometry. But the determination of the full scattering matrix is much too time consuming. We therefore propose to boost the sensitivity and resolution of scatterometry, by using an optimized  illuminating focused spot in conjunction with optimized detection schemes which both depend on the sample that is inspected. With currently available new opto-electronic spatial light modulators and deformable mirrors, the amplitude, phase and polarisation of the optimum optical fields in the entrance pupil of the focusing  objective  can be shaped position dependently to achieve a focused field that give maximum sensitivity for the nominal structure parameters. Furthermore we will optimize the detection system to retrieve the essential information at high speed and to maximally suppress the influence of the noise in the system. Since in many applications it is important to probe larger areas up to a few cm2 in a few minutes, we will design for this goal a parallelized version of the optimized illumination and detection schemes
summary_en: The characterization of nano-structures is essential in several major application areas such as in the semiconductor industry and in the recently developed plastic-based technologies. Far field optical inspection is very attractive for this purpose since it is noninvasive and can operate in-line with the production machines. In particular the technique called scatterometry is already being applied. But in order to keep up with the further developments of IC and roll-to-roll manufacturing processes, fundamental improvements of the technique are necessary. In this project, we will investigate sample-specific optimized illumination and detection to achieve maximum sensitivity and resolution. Furthermore we will optimize the detection system to achieve the required detection speed and to reduce the influence of the noise in the system. Finally, since in many applications it is important to probe larger areas up to a few cm2 in a few minutes, we will design for this goal a parallel illumination and detection system.

title: Smart integrated tips for massively parallel high-throughput atomic force microscopy
funding_scheme: Samenwerkingsprogramma High Tech Systemen en Materialen (HTSM) 2015 STW
summary_nl:
A novel concept for the design, construction and operation of an all-integrated Atomic Force Microscope (AFM) is proposed, that would enable massive parallelization for high-throughput nanometrology and nanomechanical sensing. It is based on an integrated nano-opto-electro-mechanical system (NOEMS) consisting of a semiconductor photonic crystal nanocavity realized in a double membrane structure with very sharp resonance lines, whose frequency strongly depends on the separation between the membranes. The base unit has a footprint of the order of only 15×15 μm2, and can be fabricated using state-of-the-art wafer-scale semiconductor integration technology. The outer membrane is equipped with a sharp tip, analogous to that of a conventional AFM, so that the tip-surface interaction is transferred to the membrane.
	The membrane separation is determined by electrostatic attraction, controlled by a bias voltage applied between the membranes in an electronic circuit integrated with the device. Thus the bias voltage can be used for the displacement functions of an AFM: tip-position modulation, vertical scanning of the tip, or frequency modulating the tip position. A second integrated photodetector sensitively detects the position of the tip through measurement of the cavity resonant frequency. The self-actuating and self-sensing device is optically coupled to integrated optical waveguides supplying the optical excitation from an external tunable laser. The small device footprint and the fully integrated actuation and sensing architecture enable the dense arrays of AFM ?devices to realize the massive parallelization. 	
	As a result of the seamless integration of the actuation and read-out functionalities, the tip will achieve sensitivities comparable with stand-alone AFMs with a footprint and mass orders of magnitude lower, enabling high-speed operation and massive parallelization. Indeed, the small mass provides large resonant frequencies, in the MHz range, and thereby high sensitivity and high speed of operation.
	The central goal of this project is the realization of a 5×5 array demonstrator of the concept.

title: Vital soils for sustainable intensification of agriculture
summary_nl: Voor het onderzoek op praktijkboerderijen hebben we een tijdreeks gereconstrueerd van biologische landbouwgronden die gedurende een periode tot meer dan 20 jaar geleden van gangbaar naar biologisch zijn overgegaan. Analyse van deze tijdsreeks laat zien dat de hoeveelheid en het aandeel labiele organische koolstof hoger is op biologische kleigronden dan op gangbare kleigronden, vooral in gronden met laag ijzeroxidegehalte. Tevens zien we hogere diversiteit van schimmels en lagere diversiteit van protisten. In een lange-termijn experiment was de microbiële activiteit het hoogst in biologische velden, vooral in de zomer. De multifunctionaliteit van landbouwbodems neemt af met toenemende intensiteit van het landgebruik.
summary_en: A time series was constructed of farm fields that were converted from conventional to organic farming. This time series covered more than 20 years of land-use transition to organic farming. In this time series, organic fields on clay had more labile organic carbon than conventional fields, especially in soils with low iron oxide content. Fungal diversity increases, and protist diversity decreases. In a long-term experiment, microbial activity in organic fields was higher than in conventional fields, especially in mid-summer months. The multi-functionality decreased with increasing land-use intensity.

title: OPTILIGHT: Mathematical Optimizations for Human Centric Lighting
funding_scheme: Samenwerkingsprogramma High Tech Systemen en Materialen (HTSM) 2015 STW
summary_nl:
RESEARCH SUMMARY:
The overall goal of this project is to make lighting control systems more centered towards the human user. This requires not only better insights in how humans experience light but also demands quantified models and optimization algorithms that are executed by automated lighting control systems. Despite the growing scientific understanding of the impact of light on, for instance, wellbeing, performance, circadian rhythms and sleep, benefits of this understanding cannot (yet) easily be harvested in practical systems. We lack scalable algorithms that can be used in automated systems and that can be deployed in different environments without extensive tuning by experienced lighting experts. Scalability towards broad deployment is a key sub goal of this project.

Humans want to experience light as a natural given. Having to adjust the light setting regularly is not attractive. Moreover, people are usually not aware of the longer-term effects of light so they don?t not necessarily select the optimal light setting. On the other hand, automatic controls often fail to offer a comfortable and unobtrusive natural experience and even tend to irritate people. Hence, there exists a huge gap between results obtained in controlled environments and practical deployment.  

Although control theory and optimizations using statistical signal processing are well established areas, to date they not widely used for lighting control. Yet, in audio and video processing and in gaming, models on human factors are successfully being used by automated systems. Hence we have reasons to be confident that better models human experience and perception can improve automatic control systems. However, it is not straightforward to capture human experience in equations. We believe that an important step is to better quantify the reliability of such expressions and to take this into account in probabilistic algorithms.

The project has four Work Packages (Fig 4). WP1 and WP 2 focus on obtaining better quantified models on human perception and experience. WP1 focusses on controlled experiments while WP2 takes a big data approach and extracts statistical models from observing users in natural environments. WP3 uses the quantified models and reliability information in formal optimizations. We plan to apply the principles of Statistical Signal Processing to Lighting Control and to account for incomplete knowledge that the system has about the users and learn from (hopefully) very sparse user interventions in the lighting conditions. WP4 addresses how to use this in self configuring, rapidly learning smart lighting control infrastructures.  


UTILISATION SUMMARY:
Light plays an important role in our lives. First of all, light affects people on a functional level by influencing the visibility of objects and people?s performance of visual tasks (e.g., Boyce, 2014). How well light conditions are chosen can significantly enhance or deteriorate the effectiveness of office workers (R. Cooper, 2008). Light also has a psychological effect by influencing how people feel. For instance, light can influence the subjective impression of a room (Flynn, 1977; Vogels, 2008) and people?s mood (Knez, 1995; McCloughan et al., 1999). Finally, light has an impact on biological mechanisms. Light regulates the human circadian rhythm (Duffy & Wright, 2005). Light also induces vitality and alertness (Cajochen, 2007; Smolders, de Kort & Cluitmans, 2012, 2015; Smolders, de Kort & Van den Berg, 2013). Moreover, appropriate light settings can improve sleep and avoid disorders such as Seasonal Affective Disorder (SAD) (Terman & Terman, 2005). Through these slow processes, light conditions have significant effects on wellbeing and productiveness. But ? if offered incorrectly - light itself can also be a stressor. It can cause discomfort, dissatisfaction and it can deteriorate motivation and performance (Berman et al. 1994; Rea et al. 1985; Boyce, 2014; Veitch et al. 2008).

The LED as a light source, thus as a technical means to "spray Lumens", is reaching technological maturity. This paves the way for a next wave of innovation in how we experience light and how we can dynamically adapt our environment to improve our wellbeing. LEDs allow a finer granularity of lighting control. Not only the intensity but also other parameters such as color temperature, beam size and beam shape can be set and adapted during the day. Thereby LEDs may enable significant improvements to health and wellbeing. However, in practice it turns out to be very difficult to capture these benefits. The effort to translate our knowledge about the impact of light on humans into new installations and new environments is still prohibitive and requires a lot of designs by experts and custom adaptations. 

In order to effectively valorize the outcome of the project and to ensure a transfer our results to state-of-the-art systems (see section 5.1 for our plan) the project is conducted in the context of an existing strong bilateral cooperation between TU/e and Philips in the Intelligent Lighting Institute (ILI) (see chapter 5). 

Timeliness and Urgency:
We believe that this research is urgent. Conventional lighting is rapidly being replaced by LED lighting that lasts for 50,000 hours of active on-time. Unless optimized behavior can be added to new systems in a routine fashion, this replacement will remain limited to replacing legacy by LED. So within a few years a great window of opportunity will largely have evaporated.  In parallel, over the coming decades depression and burnout will be among the primary personal, societal, health-related and economic burdens in developed countries.

title: SMART CYCLING FUTURES
funding_scheme: VerDuS Smart Urban Regions of the Future - VerDuS SURF Grote projecten
summary_nl: Cycling booms in many Dutch cities. While smart cycling innovations promise to increase cycling?s modal share in the (peri-)urban transport system even further, little is understood of their impact or cost and benefit. The ?Smart Cycling Futures (SCF)? program investigates how smart cycling innovations ─ including ICT-enabled cycling innovations, infrastructures, and social innovations like new business models ─ contribute to more resilient and liveable Dutch urban regions. Cycling innovations benefit urban regions in terms of accessibility, equality, health, liveability, and decreasing CO2-emissions when socially well embedded. To facilitate a transition to a sustainable future that respond to pressing issues, the SCF research project runs urban living labs in close collaboration with key stakeholders to develop transdisciplinary insights in the conditions needed for upscaling smart-cycling initiatives. Each living lab involving real-world experiments responds to the urgent challenges that urban regions and their stakeholders face today. The proposed research sub-programs focus on institutional dynamics, entrepreneurial strategies, governance and the socio-spatial conditions for smart cycling. Going beyond analysis, we also assess the economic, social, and spatial impacts of cycling on urban regions. The research program brings together four Dutch regions through academic institutions (three general and one applied-science universities); governmental authorities (urban and regional); and market players (innovative entrepreneurs). Together, they answer practice-based questions in a transdisciplinary and problem-oriented fashion. Research in the four regions generates both region-specific and universally applicable findings. Finally, SCF uses its strong research-practice network around cycling to co-create the research and run an outreach program.

title: HIERARCHICAL AND DISTRIBUTED OPTIMAL CONTROL OF INTEGRATED ENERGY SYSTEMS
funding_scheme: Energiesysteemintegratie - planning, operations, en sociale inbedding - compartiment 1 2015 EW
summary_nl:
For decades the main goal of the power system was to deliver power from generation plants to consumers through an extensive high-voltage transmission system and a medium to low voltage distribution system. As such the existing power system was designed in a centralized tree like fashion in order to connect a relatively small number of large plants to a large number of consumers. In addition, the gas infrastructure is developed separately, with an infrastructure consisting of high, medium and low pressure pipelines, more or less similar to the power grid structure. Both grids are regulated separately, even though they are coupled.

So far, the analysis and design of new smart energy systems in the energy infrastructure have been mainly focused on only one particular grid such as the power grid, gas grid or heat grid. In particular, the power grid has received by far the most attention. Much of the current research evolves towards embedding of renewables such as photovoltaic cells and wind power into the power grid, where it is important to take into account the cloud and wind conditions, which are less predictable than the power production of a classical power plant. In addition, there is a fine meshed gas network in the Netherlands, where embedding of biogases and/or non-natural gases is developed. Currently, this network is coupled to the power grid on a limited basis, i.e., some Combined Heat Power (CHP) systems that produce both heat and power and run on gas are embedded. Furthermore, some larger power plants operate on gas. In the future, the embedding of many more micro-CHP systems in households is foreseen, and storage of surplus electricity in the form of power-to-gas (hydrogen) is also foreseen. 

Within this research proposal we aim at developing new/tailored methods that integrate hierarchical and distributed optimal control methods for large-scale networked systems necessary for the embedding of new energy systems in the coupled power and gas grids. By a large-scale networked system, we mean a collection of interconnected heterogeneous dynamical systems (agents) sharing/collecting information. Thus, the research of this proposal is concerned with designing integrated distributed controllers (at the level of agents) based on the available limited local (asynchronous) information exchange in order to achieve a global (at the level of the entire network) hierarchical optimality criterion. To the best of our knowledge, there do not yet exist control schemes with strong theoretical foundations to ensure stability and optimality for such complex structures.

To the best of our knowledge, there do not yet exist control schemes with strong theoretical foundations to ensure stability and optimality for such complex structures.

title: Acetate as metabolic target in the prevention of overweight-related chronic metabolic disorders
summary_nl:
The connection between gut microbiota and obesity-related cardiometabolic disorders is increasingly recognized. Our gut microbiota affect the cardiometabolic phenotype by fermenting indigestible dietary components thereby producing short-chain fatty acids (SCFA). This may then affect adipose tissue function and ectopic fat storage thereby modulating insulin sensitivity. Our recent findings, using an unique design to administer acetate in the colon, show that distal, and not proximal, colonic acetate administration in healthy volunteers, in the amount achieved by a high fibre diet, has pronounced effects on lipolysis, fat oxidation and inflammatory profile. Based on this, we hypothesize that acetate when reaching a gut and systemic concentration within the high physiological range, is an important link between our gut microbiota and metabolic health by improving adipose tissue function, preventing lipid overflow and skeletal muscle fat accumulation thereby improving insulin sensitivity.
The objective of this proposal are to 1) screen which dietary fibre(s) will yield a high physiological colonic acetate concentration in ?in vitro? fermentation models, 2) investigate how key microbes are involved in a high acetate production and 3) to examine whether a dietary fibre, which yields the optimal gut and circulating acetate concentration, is able to reverse high-fat diet-induced insulin resistance (proof-of-concept study). Our approach is to use state-of-the art methodology for detailed human physiological and cellular/molecular phenotyping, microbiota composition and activity profiling in combination with ?in vitro? digestion models. The proposed studies will provide information for new strategies in nutritional prevention of insulin resistance and chronic metabolic diseases in adults and elderly.

title: Spintronic and optoelectronic nanomaterials engineered by geometrical design
summary_nl:
Nanostructured semiconducting materials are the essential building blocks of spintronic and optoelectronic devices with potential applications in spectroscopy, sensing, imaging, magnetic storage, etc. Existing functional devices, however, are generically made out of building blocks of different materials glued together in heterostructures, which intrinsically suffer of limitations due to unavoidable imperfections at interfaces and limited control in their fabrication. This proposal sets out to overcome these hurdles and aims to theoretically demonstrate how the underlying physical properties of optoelectronic and spintronic nanomaterials can be engineered by nanoscale geometrical design in single material systems. Nanostructures with curved geometries sustain elastic deformations that render inhomogeneous strain distributions affecting the local electronic properties.
I will first investigate how such inhomogeneous strain distributions in wavy ribbons of conventional semiconductor thin films, as well as of the recently isolated black phosphorus can be exploited to design new single material nanodevices for the spontaneous emission of electromagnetic radiation. Then, I will investigate how semiconducting nanostructures with helical geometries display an unprecedented strong coupling between the spin and the orbital degrees of freedom that can be exploited for spin filters more efficient than those achievable with semiconducting materials in conventional material geometries. The successful demonstration of this concept will put curved nanostructures at the forefront in the fields of spintronics and optoelectronics.

title: From active matter to artificial cells: a mechanical insight into the fabric of life
summary_nl:
The goal of the proposed research is to theoretically investigate an artificial cell-like structure to understand how mechanical functionality emerges in living matter. Living cells, from the simple prokaryotes to the more complex eukaryotes, are capable of astonishing mechanical functionalities. They can deform spontaneously or in response to environmental stimuli, move in a fluid or on a substrate and generate enough force to split themselves in two while remaining alive. These unique properties are possible because the building blocks that form the mechanical apparatus of the cell are active: they are able to transform stored or ambient energy into mechanical work. But how does functionality emerge from mechanical activity? In order to address this question I will focus on an artificial cell-like structure consisting of a lipid vesicle enclosing an active liquid crystal that performs the functions of the cytoskeleton and that can be experimentally obtained from purified extracts of cytoskeletal filaments and motor proteins (Fig. 1). Using this active prototype cell (or simply active protocell) as a model system, I will shed light into the complex mechanical properties that characterise the ?fabric of life?, via a challenging theoretical and computational research program.
Building on my expertise in continuum mechanics, liquid crystals, topological defects and geometry, I will investigate: (1) how active and passive forces allow the cell to control and modify its shape; (2) how activity and geometrical confinement can drive cell division in the absence of a regulatory network; (3) how the interactions between the cell and its environment lead to spontaneous motion and how this can be directed by chemical and hydrodynamic cues.
Our endeavours on active protocells will be complementary to the ongoing grand challenge on artificial life and will create a much needed link between the world of artificial cells and theoretical physics.

title: On-chip optomechanics experiments for quantum information processing
summary_nl: Quantum physics has been at the heart of the modern technological revolution and over the past decades ever more physical systems have been used in quantum experiments. One of the only missing entries in the zoo of quantum systems are mechanical oscillations, or phonons, which have only recently sparked renewed attention from the optomechanics community. Here photons are coupled to phonons through the radiation-pressure force, with the goal of creating macroscopic quantum states of mechanical oscillators. Despite simple proof-of-concept quantum experiments with such systems, full quantum control over phonons remains an elusive goal. In this proposal I want to use new concepts like optomechanical wavelength conversion, on-chip phonon routing, filtering, delaying and single-phonon detection to achieve full quantum control over individual phonons. This will open up completely new possibilities for quantum information processing and allow observing novel phenomena like topological phases in optomechanical systems. The research will not only have lasting impact on optomechanics and quantum physics, but will also pave the way for new technologies. My expertise in quantum optics, optomechanics and simulation and fabrication of photonic- / phononic crystals, in combination with the stimulating atmosphere and excellent research environment at the TU Delft, puts me in a unique position to realize this proposal.

title: MOSAIC: the multi-object spectrograph for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope
funding_scheme: Samenwerking FAPESP-NWO: Advanced Instrumentation for Astronomy 2015 EW
summary_nl:
With its 39m primary mirror, the ESO Extremely Large Telescope (E-ELT) will be the largest optical/near-infrared telescope ever built. MOSAIC (Multi-Object Spectrograph for Astrophysics, Inter-galactic medium studies and Cosmology) is expected to become the E-ELT's workhorse instrument for astrophysics, intergalactic medium studies and cosmology in the coming decades. MOSAIC will fully explore the large aperture and superb spatial resolution of the biggest eye on the sky. Key science cases involve searching for extra-galactic planets, resolving stellar populations in thousands of nearby galaxies, and studying high-redshift galaxies at the edge of the visible universe.

MOSAIC is a fiber-fed spectrograph, covering the telescope's full field of view with several hundred fibers and a dozen integral field units with adaptive optics capability delivering milli-arcsec spatial resolution, providing spectra ranging from the ultraviolet to the near infrared (380 - 2500 nm) at intermediate spectral resolution. The MOSAIC consortium includes scientists from Brazil, France, The Netherlands, and the United Kingdom, as main partners. Another 6 European countries are associated with the consortium at different levels. The Netherlands will be involved in designing and building the MOSAIC spectrographs; Brazil will contribute to its fiber system and spectrograph slit assembly.

This proposal aims to study and develop the fibers to spectrograph interface by producing prototype slit assemblies for MOSAIC, exchanging expertise between Brazilian and Dutch technicians and industry, and to scientifically explore state-of-the-art MOS observations to optimize the scientific and technical requirements for MOSAIC. These activities are not covered by our currently assigned budgets.

title: The Freedom of the Streets. Gender and Urban Space in Europe and Asia (1600-1850)
summary_nl:
This programme analyses the gendering of urban space in the early modern city. It is widely held that between 1600 and 1850, women gradually withdrew from the public sphere of the street and moved to the private sphere of the home. This powerful narrative, linked to theories of modernisation, has created a conceptual stranglehold that sees public space as exclusively male and private space as entirely female, thereby obscuring the actual workings of gender in pre-industrial urban societies.



This programme offers a pioneering approach to the study of gendered urban space, enabling for the first time to move beyond the public/private dichotomy and analyse women's access to pre-industrial streets in full. Through an analysis of the ownership of streets, both formally by authorities and informally through daily use, it uncovers how urban space was gendered in the run up to the nineteenth century. It hypothesises that the extent to which women could own the street depended on gender norms, local governance, urban fabric, and the everyday use of streets and squares. As such, this programme uniquely enables a cross-cultural comparison that connects the material and immaterial city, as well as for women's agency to play a central role in the analysis.



In four closely-related projects, this programme systematically compares the gendering of urban space in pre-modern Asia and Europe. Based on extensive visual and textual sources, Projects 1 and 2 provide in-depth studies of Edo and Amsterdam, two major pre-modern cities with distinct cultures, architecture, and governance. Project 3 digitally visualises gendered movement in these two cities, thereby providing a complementary spatial analysis, as well as an important tool to engage with wider audiences. Project 4 builds on Projects 1-3 and analyses how the access of women to pre-industrial streets was shaped in contrasting European and Asian urban communities.

title: SMART CYCLING FUTURES - SIA
funding_scheme: VerDuS Smart Urban Regions of the Future - VerDuS SURF Grote projecten
summary_nl: Cycling booms in many Dutch cities. While smart cycling innovations promise to increase cycling?s modal share in the (peri-)urban transport system even further, little is understood of their impact or cost and benefit. The ?Smart Cycling Futures (SCF)? program investigates how smart cycling innovations ─ including ICT-enabled cycling innovations, infrastructures, and social innovations like new business models ─ contribute to more resilient and liveable Dutch urban regions. Cycling innovations benefit urban regions in terms of accessibility, equality, health, liveability, and decreasing CO2-emissions when socially well embedded. To facilitate a transition to a sustainable future that respond to pressing issues, the SCF research project runs urban living labs in close collaboration with key stakeholders to develop transdisciplinary insights in the conditions needed for upscaling smart-cycling initiatives. Each living lab involving real-world experiments responds to the urgent challenges that urban regions and their stakeholders face today. The proposed research sub-programs focus on institutional dynamics, entrepreneurial strategies, governance and the socio-spatial conditions for smart cycling. Going beyond analysis, we also assess the economic, social, and spatial impacts of cycling on urban regions. The research program brings together four Dutch regions through academic institutions (three general and one applied-science universities); governmental authorities (urban and regional); and market players (innovative entrepreneurs). Together, they answer practice-based questions in a transdisciplinary and problem-oriented fashion. Research in the four regions generates both region-specific and universally applicable findings. Finally, SCF uses its strong research-practice network around cycling to co-create the research and run an outreach program.

title: BrainWave -- Wearable Brainwave Processing Platform
funding_scheme: Open technologieprogramma OTP oud STW 2016 STW
summary_en: In the Netherlands, ~120,000 patients are suffering from epilepsy and 40,000 patients are suffering from Parkinson’s Disease (PD). To improve the quality of life of these patients, the BrainWave project develops a wearable brainwave processing platform with a novel brainwave processor. It can reliably detect seizures in epilepsy and freezing-of-gait in Parkinson’s Disease, by continuous monitoring epilepsy and PD patients. Ultra-low-power on-chip context-aware patient-specific signal processing together with features such as data logging and cloud connection will make this brainwave processing platform wearable and suitable for non-hospital environments. BrainWave is not only beneficial for epilepsy and PD patients; it has applications in many other areas, e.g. monitoring pregnancy at home, sports, neuro rehabilitation, stroke therapy monitoring, and spasticity management. Related industry and academia will highly benefit from the new flexible and low energy platform, the developed architecture and circuit techniques for low power, and the advanced, self-learning, signal analysis techniques.

title: Collecting Suburbia
summary_nl:
Citymuseums throughout Europe are striving to improve their social significance by involving residents in the heritage of the contemporary city. Although the concept of participative museums has been well explored in presentations, collecting contemporary heritage is presenting new challenges for city museums. Museum Rotterdam would like to investigate to what extent the social aims of museums can be combined with their heritage tasks.
This research will concentrate on post-war housing culture. Museum Rotterdam already has an extensive collection relating to urban society in general. This topic also lends itself for further co-operation with the city museums of The Hague and Zoetermeer to a joint approach to contemporary culture. Furthermore, while housing culture is traditionally well represented in museums it does not adhere to insights and methods from the various scientific disciplines in the field of urban planning, lifestyle and interior.
By means of a case-study, Museum Rotterdam will focus on the geographical suburb Prins Alexander - a neighbourhood in which a range of various Dutch fashions in urban expansion can be found. An important aspect is that the pioneers of the various phases are still alive and able to participate in the investigation.
The results of the initial research phase will be presented in an exhibition. This exhibition will then form the basis for the final research phase in which the input from scholars, museum professionals, residents and the general public will provide insights into the potential and consequences of the various contemporary methods of collecting suburbia.

title: Het ontwikkelen van statistische vaardigheden via histogrammen
summary_nl: Leerlingen in het voortgezet onderwijs zijn niet goed in staat verantwoorde conclusies te trekken uit statistische data. Dit probleem speelt zelfs bij eenvoudige grafische representaties van data zoals het histogram. De onderzoeksvraag is hoe leerlingen kunnen leren om correcte conclusies te trekken uit histogrammen. Via eye-tracking wordt nagegaan wat de fouten bij leerlingen veroorzaakt. Op basis van de resultaten hiervan wordt een interventie ontworpen die leerlingen ondersteunt om correcte conclusies te trekken. De effectiviteit van deze interventie wordt gemeten. Dit onderzoek levert een bijdrage aan theorievorming over grafische representaties en aan verbetering van het statistiekonderwijs voor havo en vwo.

title: To be ready or not for glucose challenges; a critical role for the brain?'s reward center
summary_nl: De hersenen zijn belangrijk voor regulatie van de bloedsuikerspiegel. Onverwacht is gebleken dat het beloningsgebied in de hersenen belangrijk voor motivationeel gedrag, suiker kan detecteren en de bloedsuikerspiegel kan beïnvloeden. Dit project onderzoekt hoe en wanneer dit hersengebied dit reguleert, en hoe kennis kan worden gebruikt voor betere behandeling van suikerziekte.
summary_en: The brain is key for  proper blood sugar levels regulation. Unexpectedly, it has been found that the reward area in the brain important for motivational behavior can detect sugar and influence blood sugar levels. This project investigates how and when this brain region regulates this, and how knowledge can be used for better treatment of diabetes.
