title: Quantum gases with strong interactions
summary_nl: De zeer dichte kern van een neutronenster bestaat uit sterk wisselwerkende deeltjes. De onderzoekers bootsen dezelfde condities na op aarde in een ultrakoud quantum gas, dat onder deze condities bestaat uit een soep van superfluide atomen, dimeer en trimeer moleculen. Het onderzoek draagt bij aan de fundamentele kennis van sterk-gecorreleerde quantum systemen, en aan de ontwikkeling van nieuwe quantummaterialen en quantumcomputers gebaseerd op neutrale atomen.
summary_en: The very dense core of a neutron star consists of strongly interacting particles. The researchers simulate the same conditions on Earth in an ultra-cold quantum gas, which under these conditions consists of a soup of superfluid atoms, dimer and trimer molecules. The research contributes to the fundamental knowledge of highly correlated quantum systems, and to the development of new quantum materials and quantum computers based on neutral atoms.

title: Understanding structural heterogeneities in Deep Eutectic Solvents and Ionic Liquids
summary_nl: Deep Eutectic Solvents (DESs) en Ionic Liquids (ILs) krijgen steeds meer belangstelling vanwege hun uitstekende eigenschappen als oplosmiddel, zeer lage dampdruk en onbrandbaarheid. Daarom worden ze vaak gekwalificeerd als "groene" oplosmiddelen en worden ze beschouwd als een vervanging voor conventionele organische oplosmiddelen die momenteel in de industrie worden gebruikt. Deep Eutectic solvents en ionische vloeistoffen hebben een fascinerende microstructuur vanwege het samenspel tussen hydrofobe en hydrofiele interacties. Dit beïnvloedt de thermofysische eigenschappen van deze complexe vloeistoffen. Met geavanceerde computersimulaties hebben we inzicht verkregen in deze microstructuur en ontrafeld hoe deze de eigenschappen van deze vloeistoffen beïnvloedt.
summary_en: Deep Eutectic Solvents (DESs) and Ionic Liquids (ILs) are attracting increasing interest due to their excellent solvent properties, very low vapor pressure, and non-flammability. Therefore, they are often qualified as "green" solvents and are considered as a replacement for conventional organic solvents presently used in industry. Deep Eutectic Solvents and Ionic Liquids have a fascinating microstructure due to the interplay between hydrophobic and hydrophilic interactions. This influences the thermophysical properties of these complex fluids. Using advanced computer simulations, we have obtained insight in this microstructure and have unravelled how this influences the properties of these fluids.

title: Evaluatie van de vernieuwing vmbo 2016-2022
funding_scheme: NRO ProBO Evaluatie van de vernieuwing van het vmbo
summary_nl:
In 2011 is gestart met de vernieuwing van de beroepsgerichte leerwegen in het vmbo. Door de vernieuwing komen er straks tien examenprogramma’s met bijbehorende profielen, wordt loopbaanoriëntatie en –begeleiding (LOB) onderdeel van de examenprogramma’s en omvatten alle profielen een kern, profielmodulen en vrije keuzevakken. 



In schooljaar 2016-2017 worden de beroepsgerichte examenprogramma’s landelijk ingevoerd. Scholen mogen vanaf dan, en moeten vanaf schooljaar 2017/18, hun onderwijsprogramma in het derde leerjaar aanbieden volgens de nieuwe structuur en eindtermen. 



Op verzoek van OCW wordt een beleidsmatige evaluatie van de vernieuwing uitgevoerd. Het onderzoek gaat na hoe scholen de vernieuwing invoeren, tot welke resultaten dat leidt en in hoeverre de vernieuwingsdoelstellingen daarmee worden bereikt. Het onderzoek is zo opgezet dat het tussentijds aanbevelingen oplevert voor beleidsmakers en scholen en andere betrokkenen ondersteunt bij het implementatieproces.



De volgende vragen staan centraal: 



1.      Wat houdt de vernieuwing van het vmbo in? Welke interventies worden ingezet, welke uitkom-sten worden verwacht en waarom? (Reconstructie beleidstheorie: deelonderzoek 1)

2.      Op welke wijze implementeren scholen de interventies, waarom doen zij dat zo, en hoe verloopt die implementatie? (Procesevaluatie: deelonderzoek 2)

3.      Tot welke opbrengsten leidt de vernieuwing van het vmbo? (Jaarlijkse monitor, vinger aan de pols: deelonderzoek 3)

4.      Welke mechanismen verklaren de opbrengsten van de vernieuwing van het vmbo en welke con-textvariabelen zijn daarbij van belang? (Verklarende evaluatie: deelonderzoek 4)

5.      Welke effecten kunnen worden toegeschreven aan de beleidswijziging in het algemeen en de in-voeringsstrategieën van scholen in het bijzonder? (Effectevaluatie: deelonderzoek 5).

title: Kristallijne zonnecellen in composiet
summary_nl: Het midden- en kleinbedrijf (mkb) wil graag zonne-energie integreren in hun eindproducten om te verduurzamen en om hun marktpositie te versterken. Het bestaande aanbod van fotovoltaïsche (PV) zonnecellen in zonnepanelen sluit echter niet aan bij de eisen en wensen van het mkb waardoor integratie in hun eindproducten onmogelijk is. Gezien de lage kosten en hoge efficienties, zijn kristallijne zonnecellen een geschikte kandidaat voor het mkb, mits een nieuwe moduletechnologie ontwikkeld wordt. Idealiter is deze nieuwe moduletechnologie op basis van composieten, omdat deze voldoende vormvrijheid en flexibiliteit bieden. In de ontwikkeling van een nieuwe moduletechologie is de interconnectie van cellen en modules ook van belang: kennis die het mkb moet ontwikkelen. Een goede interconnectie waarborgt een hoog rendement en grote vormvrijheid van de modules. Om het mkb hierin te ondersteunen, is het project Kristallijne zonnecellen in composiet gelanceerd. Samen met 12 mkb'ers, een branchevereniging en drie kennisinstellingen wordt in 4 werkpakketten, respectievelijk interconnectie, encapsulatie, evaluatie, projectmanagement, onderzoek gedaan naar de integratie van kristallijne zonnecellen in eindproducten van composiet. Het beoogde doel van het project is opbouw van kennis van encapsulatie van kristallijne zonnecellen en het aantonen van een proof-of-principle in het werkpakket interconnectie en encapsulatie. Het proof-of-principle moet aantonen dat kristallijne zonnecellen goed geïntegreerd kunnen worden in composietmaterialen, zoals die worden gebruikt binnen het mkb. Om het eindproduct te beoordelen, wordt een testprotocol ontwikkeld om kristallijne zonnecellen in composietmaterialen te karakteriseren in het werkpakket evaluatie. De ervaringen die worden opgedaan, worden vastgelegd in een handleiding met een set richtlijnen, wat bedrijven kan helpen kristallijne zonnecellen te integreren in hun producten. Het vastleggen van de richtlijnen gebeurt, samen met het algemene projectmanagement, in het werkpakket projectmanagement. Daarnaast wordt een protocol ontwikkeld om de nieuwe kristallijne fotovoltaïsche (PV)-module technologie te evalueren. Het resultaat zal ertoe leiden dat het mkb praktische kennis heeft om kristallijne zonncellen in hun half-fabrikaten te integreren.

title: Circulaire rundermest
summary_nl:
Dit voorstel getiteld ?Circulaire Rundermest? staat een integrale aanpak voor ogen van de mestproblematiek in de melkveehouderij. Een consortium van MKB bedrijven wil samen met de Vilentum Hogeschool de eerste stappen zetten om bij te dragen aan een duurzame oplossing voor de Nederlandse mestproblematiek en toekomstige fosfaatschaarste. Het oplossen van het Nederlandse mestoverschot is cruciaal voor de overleving van de veehouderijsector in Nederland. In combinatie daarbij tevens de (toekomstige) schaarste aan fosfaat oplossen is een kans voor de Nederlandse landbouw. Gezien de ervaringen uit het verleden rondom de mestproblematiek wordt de aanpak gericht op marktconforme producten maken uit het mestoverschot, in plaats van de afvalbenadering, waarbij uitgegaan wordt van het circulaire gedachtegoed. Andere unieke aspecten in dit traject zijn i) de applicatie van een nieuwe high-tech scheidingstechnologie en ii) gebruikmaking van nieuwe combinaties van bestaande bioraffinage-technieken. Er wordt gestreefd naar het produceren van minimaal twee eindproducten: i) een anorganische fosfaat rijke fractie en ii) een organische fosfaatarme fractie. Deze fracties voldoen aan alle kwaliteitseisen om in de markt toegepast te worden als fosfor/fosfaatmeststof en bodemverbeteraar.

Om dit te bereiken wordt door middel van praktijkgericht onderzoek antwoord gegeven op de onderzoeksvraag: ?Welke combinaties van bioraffinage-technieken zijn duurzaam en effectief voor het synthetiseren marktconforme fosfor/fosfaatconcentraten en organische stof producten uit rundermest??

Op basis van ervaringen uit de praktijk en opgedane kennis bij de betrokken lectoraten en de projectpartners wordt een conceptueel raffinage proces ontworpen. Dit proces wordt vervolgens in deelstappen experimenteel getoetst zowel bij de deelnemend MKB als bij de aangesloten hogescholen. Het optimale design wordt tenslotte in de praktijk getoetst door samenwerking van de aangesloten MKB projectpartners. Dit totaal wordt gecomplementeerd met economische en ecologische analyses ter vergelijking met bestaande systemen van de gemaakte keuzes. Relevante uitkomsten voor de sector over marktconforme producten en best presterende scheidingstechnieken worden onder andere via (vak)publicaties en een symposia verspreid.

Deze fracties voldoen aan alle kwaliteitseisen om in de markt toegepast te worden als fosfor/fosfaatmeststof en bodemverbeteraar.

Om dit te bereiken wordt door middel van praktijkgericht onderzoek antwoord gegeven op de onderzoeksvraag: ?Welke combinaties van bioraffinage-technieken zijn duurzaam en effectief voor het synthetiseren marktconforme fosfor/fosfaatconcentraten en organische stof producten uit rundermest??

Op basis van ervaringen uit de praktijk en opgedane kennis bij de betrokken lectoraten en de projectpartners wordt een conceptueel raffinage proces ontworpen. Dit proces wordt vervolgens in deelstappen experimenteel getoetst zowel bij de deelnemend MKB als bij de aangesloten hogescholen. Het optimale design wordt tenslotte in de praktijk getoetst door samenwerking van de aangesloten MKB projectpartners. Dit totaal wordt gecomplementeerd met economische en ecologische analyses ter vergelijking met bestaande systemen van de gemaakte keuzes. Relevante uitkomsten voor de sector over marktconforme producten en best presterende scheidingstechnieken worden onder andere via (vak)publicaties en een symposia verspreid.

title: Teaching Technology, primary approach
summary_nl: Op basis van Evidence-Based Design ontwikkelden wij richtlijnen voor valide, op handelen gebaseerde taken, waarmee inzicht in eenvoudige technische systemen vastgesteld kan worden bij leerlingen van 9 tot 12 jaar. Leraren hebben de neiging om de technische vaardigheden van hun leerlingen te onderschatten en die van meisjes in het bijzonder. Een cursus over vaardigheidsontwikkeling met deze taken bleek een positieve invloed te hebben op het diagnostisch vermogen van leraren. Het formatief gebruik van de taken werd positief gewaardeerd door leerlingen. Het evaluatief gebruik toonde aan dat alleen leerlingen met beperkte voorkennis profiteren van praktische taken zonder instructie en feedback.
summary_en: Based on Evidence-Based Design, we developed guidelines for valid, action-based tasks that can be used to gain insight into 9 to 12-year-old pupils’ understanding of simple technical systems. Teachers tend to underestimate the technical skills of their students and those of girls in particular. A course on skill development with these tasks positively affected the diagnostic ability of teachers. Formative use positively affected perceived challenge adequacy. Evaluative use showed that only students with limited prior knowledge benefit from practical tasks without instruction and feedback.

title: HR matching - molecular pathotyping of parasitic nematodes to maximize agronomic life span of non-hosts and host plant resistances
funding_scheme: Open technologieprogramma OTP oud STW 2016 STW
summary_nl:
Fertile arable soils are among the most precious and basic commodities on our planet as they are indispensible for the production of food, feed and fiber. Soil is teeming with life, and the soil living community provides essential functions such as carbon and nutrient cycling, and water retention. The condition of the soil living community is gradually declining at a global scale, mainly due to large-scale, single crop production systems in combination with non-durable agricultural practices. For food production at an affordable price, large scale mono-crop production systems are unavoidable, but pathogens thrive is such systems. For decades wide-spectrum pesticides have been used especially for below-ground pathogen control. Because of their highly negative impact on the environment, most of these wide-spectrum pesticides have been or will be phased out(not just in the European Union but worldwide. With an estimated damage of $US 125 billion per year [1], plant-parasitic nematodes are probably the most harmful category of soil pathogens. Mainly because of their limited mobility in soil and their low number of generations per year, host plant resistances are a remarkably durable means to manage of this category of pathogens. The fundament of host plant resistances is the recognition of the pathogen by the plant. Knowledge about the virulence determinants of individual plant-parasitic nematode species is essential to predict the effectiveness of host plant resistances. Fast and affordable diagnostic assays for the determination of virulence characteristics of plant-parasitic nematodes are required to fully exploit the control potential of resistant varieties and non-hosts. Currently, diagnostics for virulence characteristics compatible with practical applications are non-existent. 
	To manipulate their hosts, plant-parasitic nematodes secrete a diverse repertoire of proteins, so-called effectors. To evade being recognized by highly specific resistance proteins in host plants, parasitic nematodes constantly modify their effectors and this process has resulted in enormous expansion of effector gene families. Hence, virulence determinants of plant-parasitic nematodes should be sought among (a) expanded gene families, showing (b) diversifying selection, and encoding proteins (c) harboring secretion signals. In this project, we will use a field pathogenomics approach to identify members of effector families that trigger three, commercially highly relevant resistances in potato: the H1 gene against two pathotypes of the potato cyst nematode (PCN) Globodera rostochiensis, Grp1 conferring resistance against a G. rostochiensis and a G. pallida pathotype, and Rmc1, a major R gene against the Columbian root-knot nematode Meloidogyne chitwoodi. By exploiting the same principles, we will pinpoint effectors that determine host plant specificities of races of the stem nematode Ditylenchus dipsaci, a major pathogen in horticulture (including flower bulbs). Based on our preliminary data with a tropical root knot nematode, we foresee that criteria a, b and c will result about 15 candidate virulence-determining gene families per nematode species. Targeted PCR amplification of these families followed by next generation sequencing in a range of well-characterized populations will provide insight in environment-exposed, variable protein domains that tightly correlate with resistance protein activation and, in case of the stem nematode, host preference. Effector domain variations that determine recognition by selected resistance proteins, or - in case of races of stem nematodes - host preferences, will serve as the very basis for affordable and specific quantitative PCR assays that will allow full exploitation of the control potential of resistant and non-host plant genotypes.
summary_en: Fertile arable soils are a precious and very basic commodity as the production of food, feed and fiber almost completely depends on their proper biological functioning. Large-scale mono-crop production systems provide hundreds of millions of people with food at an affordable price, but they are highly vulnerable to plant pathogens. Soil-borne plant pathogens have been controlled for decades by nonselective fumigants with a highly negative impact on human health and the environment. In most parts of the world, the use of these generic biocides is either severely restricted or fully banned, hence there is an urgent need for alternative control handles. Root parasitic roundworms (‘nematodes’) are by far the most urgent threat to food production. Due to peculiarities of their biology (e.g. low dispersal rates, low number of generations per year), host and non-host resistances constitute a remarkably durable way to manage this category of soil-borne diseases. Host plant resistances are available, but no tools are available to match pathogen populations (“pathotypes” or “races”) with the right host plant resistances. The goal of this project is to develop affordable, high-throughput DNA-based assays for the identification of pathotypes and races of four major plant-parasitic nematode species, a prerequisite for the right matching between pathogens and available host plants resistances.

Understanding the occurrence of oxygen deficiency can explain global patterns in biodiversity and provide insights into the effects of climate change.

title: Do mycorrhizal fungi mediate soil carbon fate?
summary_nl:
Koolstofvastlegging in de bodem is een belangrijk maar nauwelijks begrepen mechanisme dat een tegenwicht vormt voor de atmosferische CO2-emissies en daarmee de klimaatverandering. Een belangrijke biotische determinant van koolstoftransformaties is mycorrhiza, een plant-schimmelsymbiose die wordt gekenmerkt door bijna alle vaatplanten op aarde. Mycorrhizae hebben verschillende vormen, waarvan arbusculaire en ectomycorrhizae (AM en EM) de meest voorkomende zijn.

Met behulp van grondige experimenten en modellering vult dit project de belangrijkste kennisleemte met betrekking tot processen van koolstofaccumulatie in de bodem: om te onthullen of en hoe AM- en EM-schimmels een verschillende invloed hebben op de koolstofcyclus in de bodem.
summary_en:
Soil carbon sequestration is an important but hardly  understood mechanism counterbalancing atmospheric CO2 emissions and thereby climate change. An important biotic determinant of soil carbon transformations is mycorrhiza, a plant-fungal symbiosis featured by nearly all vascular plants on Earth. Mycorrhizae have different forms, among which arbuscular and ectomycorrhiza (AM and EM) are the most wide-spread. 

Using thorough experimentation and modeling, this project fillss the principle knowledge gap with regard to soil carbon accumulation processes: to reveal if and how AM and EM fungi differently affect soil carbon cycling.

title: 3D spectro-microscopy for understanding mass transport processes in catalyst bodies of complex porosity
summary_nl: Vaste katalysatoren, materialen die gebruikt worden voor de productie van onze brandstoffen en materialen van alle dag, zijn poreus. Om te begrijpen hoe de complexe poriestructuur van katalysatoren - met poriën 100-10000 keer kleiner dan een mensenhaar - de prestaties beïnvloedt, hebben we methoden ontwikkeld om dergelijke kleine porienetwerken in 3D af te beelden met behulp van röntgenmicroscopie en single-molecule-fluorescentiemicroscopie. We kunnen porienetwerken nu in 3D in kaart brengen met ongekende ruimtelijke resolutie en een individueel lichtgevend molecuul volgen dat er doorheen reist. Hieruit verkregen informatie kan aanleiding geven tot nieuwe en/of verbeterde katalysatoren, bijvoorbeeld voor het hergebruik van kunststofafval.
summary_en: Many materials used today are made using functional porous materials such as solid catalysts. To understand how a solid catalyst's complex pore structure - with pores that are 100-10000 times smaller than a human hair - affects their performance we developed methods to image such tiny pore networks in 3D using X-ray microscopy and single molecule fluorescence microscopy. We can now map such a pore network in 3D at unprecedented spatial resolution and follow an individual light-emitting molecule traveling through. Information obtained from this can trigger new and/or improved applications/design of catalysts, for example using them in plastic waste recycling.

title: Compliant Gyroscopic Actuators for Minimalistic Wearable Robotics
summary_nl:
Exoskeletons have the tantalizing potential to enable paralyzed patients to walk again, or to make healthy people stronger or faster. But only in science fictions movies do people actually move around naturally in robotic suits: the conventional approach has left us with cumbersome and heavy prototypes. One of the main bottlenecks is the actuation principle: powerful, heavy actuators to generate the required joint moments, which intrinsically requires attachment to multiple segments of the user's body. 
What if we could make robotic actuation wearable, lightweight, and so unobtrusive it is not even noticeable as an aid? I will realize the much-needed breakthrough in wearable robotic actuation by harnessing the gyroscopic effects of fast-spinning flywheels into small lightweight actuators that do not require any exoskeletal structure. For example, they can be placed at foot level while supporting the hip during the swing phase of gait. The idea has never been realized because fast spinning masses do not only provide a means of actuation, but they also represent a substantial source of undesired and disturbing (parasitic) moments in response to unforeseen rotations - which abound when interacting with humans in realistic environments. The innovation to tackle this issue is a new mechanical concept that introduces an additional gimbal with passive compliance to the conventional control moment gyroscope design. By means of this mechanism, moments can be measured and controlled finely, and parasitic moments can be avoided fully via control and also via mechanical protection. 
This concept may bring about a breakthrough for wearable actuation, ultimately enabling new healthcare applications like wearable balance assistance for users with increased risk of falls, and active above-knee prosthetics with superior performance. My gyroscopic actuators will pave the way for the much-awaited introduction of wearable robotic technology that improves mobility, independence and health.

title: Scalable quantum computation at practical temperatures
summary_nl:
Quantum computation holds the promise of solving problems that are unsolvable with classical methods. However, the construction of a quantum computer is extremely demanding and requires thousands of interacting qubits with exquisite control. Silicon can come to the rescue and serve as an ideal platform technology for qubit operation. I have recently demonstrated single-qubit and two-qubit gates with silicon quantum dot qubits. This opens prospects for scalability, as these silicon qubits can be constructed with proven technology capable of producing billions of conventional transistors on a single chip. 

My goal is to push the qubit performance beyond thresholds necessary for quantum computation and to increase the number of qubits such that large arrays come in sight. A major engineering challenge and paradigm shift, is to raise the operating temperature of high-performance quantum dot qubits to four Kelvin, where cooling power is sufficient to cope with the heat dissipation of larger qubit circuits.

To reach this goal, I will focus on the following key steps. First, my team will diminish quantum errors due to electrical noise such that the qubit performance drastically improves. I propose a novel industry-compatible method for quantum dot fabrication, which will reduce the noise while the sensitivity to noise will be reduced by eliminating spin-orbit coupling. Second, we will isolate the spin states that define the qubits from other degrees of freedom, such that we can increase the operation temperature. Third, we will transport spin states between quantum dots, resulting in benchmarks for spin relaxation-lengths in the solid state and the demonstration of long-range qubit coupling. 

These steps enable us to perform quantum error-correction on a qubit array, providing the path to engineer a logical qubit and taking us into an era where arbitrarily long quantum computations can be performed.

title: The unknown role of Submarine canyons ? Pathways or sinks for Organic Carbon? (BYPASS?)
summary_nl:
Dr. F. (Furu) Mienis (v)

NIOZ Netherlands Institute for Sea Research

Het belang bepalen voor transport van koolstof via onderwater canyons tussen kust en diepzee en de rol van canyons als (tijdelijke) koolstofopslag. Koolstofopslag via lateraal transport is een nog onbekende factor in de wereldwijde mariene koolstofcyclus, die weer bepalend is voor ons klimaat.
summary_en:
Dr. F. (Furu) Mienis (f)

NIOZ Netherlands Institute for Sea Research

We aim to determine the role of submarine canyons as pathway in carbon transport from shallow water depths to the deep sea. In addition their role as carbon sink is studied. The lateral transport of carbon is a so far understudied part in the global marine carbon cycle, while it can have a major impact on global climate.

title: Preparing MFDEs for the Modelling World
summary_nl:
The abstract world of calculus with its continuous space-time variables frequently clashes with the real world,
where discreteness in some shape or form can play an important role. For example, nerve fibers have a myeline coating that admits gaps at regular intervals. These gaps can block signals from propagating through the fiber, but are ignored by many classical conduction models. In order to study the growth of plants, one must take into account that cells divide and grow in a fashion that is influenced heavily by the spatial configuration of their neighbours. Even classical differential equations need to be discretized before computer simulations can be run.


Motivated by considerations of this type, an increasing interest has arisen in mathematical modelling techniques that reflect the underlying spatial and/or temporal discreteness. By now it is well-known that
such models can capture intriguing dynamical behaviour
that their continuous counterparts can not. Unfortunately, rigorous attempts to explain this behaviour invariably lead to significant mathematical complexities that need to be addressed.

We pay this price here by handling differential equations
that include both forward- and backward-looking terms. Such equations are called functional differential equations of mixed type (MFDEs) and are notoriously challenging to analyze. Indeed, many traditional mathematical tools such as phase plane analyses, semigroups and variation-of-constants formula's fail to work for MFDEs, which are infinite-dimensional and ill-posed.

The PI has made some key contributions towards the harnessing of MFDEs by adapting modern machinery such as exponential splittings, pointwise Green's functions and exchange Lemma's for use in this setting. With this proposal
we aim not only to continue and accelerate this trend, but also to translate our new technical mathematical insights
into powerful tools that are attractive to the modelling community.
summary_en:
The abstract world of calculus with its continuous space-time variables frequently clashes with the real world,
where discreteness in some shape or form can play an important role. For example, nerve fibers have a myeline coating that admits gaps at regular intervals. These gaps can block signals from propagating through the fiber, but are ignored by many classical conduction models. In order to study the growth of plants, one must take into account that cells divide and grow in a fashion that is influenced heavily by the spatial configuration of their neighbours. Even classical differential equations need to be discretized before computer simulations can be run.


Motivated by considerations of this type, an increasing interest has arisen in mathematical modelling techniques that reflect the underlying spatial and/or temporal discreteness. By now it is well-known that
such models can capture intriguing dynamical behaviour
that their continuous counterparts can not. Unfortunately, rigorous attempts to explain this behaviour invariably lead to significant mathematical complexities that need to be addressed.

We pay this price here by handling differential equations
that include both forward- and backward-looking terms. Such equations are called functional differential equations of mixed type (MFDEs) and are notoriously challenging to analyze. Indeed, many traditional mathematical tools such as phase plane analyses, semigroups and variation-of-constants formula's fail to work for MFDEs, which are infinite-dimensional and ill-posed.

The PI has made some key contributions towards the harnessing of MFDEs by adapting modern machinery such as exponential splittings, pointwise Green's functions and exchange Lemma's for use in this setting. With this proposal
we aim not only to continue and accelerate this trend, but also to translate our new technical mathematical insights
into powerful tools that are attractive to the modelling community.

title: Explicit teaching of text-structural features in primary education
summary_nl: Vaardige lezers gebruiken de tekststructuur om tot diep tekstbegrip te komen. In dit project onderzochten we daarom wat de meerwaarde is van tekststructuuronderwijs (TO) in de Nederlandse context. Uit onze meta-analyse blijkt dat TO positieve effecten heeft op tekstbegrip, onthouden, samenvatten en tekststructuurkennis van leerlingen in groep 6-8. Aangezien ons stand-van-zaken-onderzoek uitwijst dat het Nederlandse leescurriculum weinig aandacht besteedt aan TO, hebben we via ontwerpgericht onderzoek TO-materialen ontwikkeld en getest, en via effectonderzoek de meerwaarde daarvan laten zien. Ook hebben we aangetoond dat implementatie in de Nederlandse context vraagt om verdere ontwikkeling van materialen en om professionalisering van leerkrachten.
summary_en: Proficient readers make predictions about text content on the basis of the text structure, how main ideas are organized. This dissertation examines whether explicit text structure instruction can foster primary school students' reading comprehension skills. Our meta-analysis shows positive effects of text structure instruction (TSI). Still, the Dutch reading comprehension curriculum pays little attention to TSI. In a design-based research, an intervention study, and a multiple-case study we show the possibilities and positive effects of TSI in the Dutch context, as well as the obstacles that need to be overcome in terms of developing suitable educational materials and teacher professionalization.

title: Training the Circadian Rhythm: Conditioning of the Cortisol Awakening Response
summary_nl: Slaap is van grote invloed op de gezondheid en wordt grotendeels bepaald door automatische hormonale processen. Onderzoek toont aan dat fysiologische processen te beïnvloeden zijn door leerprocessen, zoals conditionering. In ons onderzoek passen we dit proces toe op het interne 24-uursritme en het hormoon cortisol door te conditioneren tijdens de slaap. Op het snijvlak van psychologie en fysiologie kijken we naar de complexe relaties tussen leren, slaap, vermoeidheid en stress. De resultaten zullen aantonen of we cortisolniveaus en de biologische klok via leerprocessen kunnen beïnvloeden en interventies ontwikkelen voor stoornissen op het gebied van stress, cortisolstofwisseling en het dag-nachtritme.
summary_en: Sleep is an important part of health and is largely determined by automatic hormonal processes. Research shows that physiological processes can be influenced by learning processes such as conditioning. In our research we apply this process to the internal diurnal (24-hour) rhythm and the hormone cortisol by conditioning during sleep. Combining insights from psychology and physiology, we examine the complex relationships between learning, sleep, fatigue and stress. The results will indicate if we could influence cortisol levels and the diurnal rhythm by learning and develop interventions for many disorders related to stress, cortisol metabolism and the diurnal rhythm.

title: Vitamins for proteins: equipping enzymes with new cofactors
summary_nl: Ieder organisme is afhankelijk van de werking van enzymen. Deze natuurlijke moleculaire machines bevatten behalve eiwit ook meestal een hulpstof, een zogenaamde cofactor. Enzym cofactoren kunnen beschouwd worden als vitamines voor cellen. In dit project is de rol van een recent ontdekte cofactor (deazaflavine) onderzocht. Hierbij is specifiek onderzocht of de enzymen die deze cofactor gebruiken toegepast kunnen worden in de biotechnologie.
summary_en: In nature, virtually every chemical reaction is catalysed by enzymes. These protein-based catalysts often contain helper molecules, so-called cofactors, which assist in catalysis. Hence, cofactors extend the scope of chemistry in nature beyond that what is feasible when using only the twenty naturally occurring amino acids. In this project, a newly discovered class of cofactor-dependent enzymes, the deazaflavin-dependent enzymes, has been explored for biotechnological applications.

title: Learning to listen. The transformation of concert culture in Dutch musical capitals in the nineteenth century
funding_scheme: Promoties in de geesteswetenschappen PGW 2016 GW
summary_nl:
Waarom begon men in de negentiende eeuw op een fundamenteel andere manier naar concertmuziek te luisteren? Het Europese concertleven ontwikkelde drastisch in deze eeuw en het concertpubliek leerde naar muziek te luisteren zoals nog steeds de norm is in onze huidige 

maatschappij. Dit promotieproject bestudeert de opkomst van deze luisterpraktijk in de context van veranderende concertculturen in Amsterdam, Den Haag, Utrecht en Rotterdam. Hiervoor analyseer ik ontwikkelingen in 1) programmeringsconventies, 2) uitvoeringspraktijken en 3) publiekservaringen

als resultaat van lokale, nationale en transnationale interacties van en tussen concertorganisatoren, musici, critici en publieksgroepen.
summary_en: Why did people start to listen to music in a fundamentally different way during the nineteenth century? European concert life transformed in this century and concert audiences learned to listen to music as is still the norm in our present day society. This PhD project studies the emergence of this listening practice in the context of changing concert cultures in Amsterdam, The Hague, Utrecht and Rotterdam. The project traces the developments in 1) programming conventions, 2) performance practices and 3) audience experiences as a result of local, national and transnational interactions by and between concert organizers, musicians, critics and audiences.

title: Alliance for Responsible Denim
summary_nl:
The denim industry faces many complex sustainability challenges and has been especially criticized for its polluting and hazardous production practices. Reducing resource use of water, chemicals and energy and changing denim production practices calls for collaboration between various stakeholders, including competing denim brands. There is great benefit in combining denim brands’ resources and knowledge so that commonly defined standards and benchmarks are developed and realized on a scale that matters. Collaboration however, and especially between 

competitors, is highly complex and prone to fail. 



This project brings leading denim brands together to collectively take initial steps towards improving the ecological sustainability impact of denim production, particularly by establishing measurements, benchmarks and standards for resource use (e.g. chemicals, water, energy) and creating best practices for effective collaboration. The central research question of our project is: How do denim brands effectively collaborate together to create common, industry standards on resource use and benchmarks for improved ecological sustainability in denim production? To answer this question, we will use a mixed-method, action research approach. The project’s research setting is the Amsterdam Metropolitan Area (MRA), which has a strong denim cluster and is home to many international denim brands and start-ups.

title: Het functioneren van de Nederlandse militaire inlichtingendienst gedurende de dekolonisatiestrijd in Nederlands-Indië 1945-1949
summary_nl:
Het onderzoek beoogt de hele Nederlandse inlichtingencomponent (NEFIS/CMI) in Nederlands-Indië tijdens de dekolonisatieoorlog onder de loep te nemen en de relatie tussen inlichtingen en beleid te onderzoeken. De hoofdvraag luidt: hoe was de verhouding tussen inlichtingen en beleid gedurende de dekolonisatiestrijd in Nederlands-Indië? Was intelligence vooral beleidsondersteunend of ook richtinggevend?

Het theoretische kader wordt gevormd door de drie varianten met betrekking tot de relatie tussen intelligence en policy, geformuleerd door Amerikaanse en Britse auteurs. Daarbij is van belang hoe de zogenaamde ‘intelligence cycle’ functioneerde. Onderzocht zal worden bij welke variant het handelen van de Nederlandse inlichtingendiensten het meest past.

title: Light. Catalyst. ACTION!
summary_nl:
Perovskite solar cells (PSC's) are an attractive photovoltaic material due to their extremely cheap cost and simple fabrication methods, and have rapidly achieved efficiencies above 20%.  However, PSC's are highly unstable during operational conditions, thus limiting their immediate real-world applications.  In this proposal, I will develop new techniques to probe the photo-induced degradation of PSC's that will provide new insights and potential methods to overcome their instability.  Specifically, I will use a physical vapour co-evaporation technique to create novel architectures and compositions of methyl ammonia lead iodide (MAPI) perovskites that directly confront the deleterious defect structure of these materials.

	In addition, storing the solar energy converted to electricity by PSC's via the photo-driven electrolysis of water offers a sustainable pathway towards a renewable and clean energy future.  However, the current state-of-the-art water oxidation and reduction catalysts are made from expensive rare-earth metals that are not viable for practical upscaling or utilization.  Therefore, in this proposal, I will also develop novel hydrogen and oxygen evolution catalysts made from earth abundant materials to replace their precious metal counterparts.  To achieve this goal, I will use several in-situ spectroelectrochemical techniques to probe the reaction pathways on highly efficient electrocatalyst materials, and replicate this behavior on innovative new materials.  This approach will provide new insights and mechanistic understanding for electrochemical water splitting materials to enable the development of novel catalysts.

	My extensive experience in the field of photoelectrocatalysis, specifically in the defect engineering of physical vapour deposited semiconductors and in-situ characterization of electrocatalysts, make me an ideal candidate to carry out the proposed research in this project.  The insights gained in this proposal will lead to a better understanding of promising photovoltaic and electrocatalyst materials that will enable a scientific and technological progress of solar fuel production, which will be unique in the world.

title: Metaphorical Meanings for Artificial Agents
summary_nl: The ability to understand analogy and metaphor is fundamental to human intelligence and creativity. Modelling analogy and metaphor effectively will enable us to model human language, contributing to technological advancements that can be integrated with the kind of artefact that humans use on an everyday basis, such as mobile phones or wearable tech. My research combines methods from computational linguistics, category theory, and conceptual spaces to develop a model of metaphorical meaning. The research will build on the compositional distributional model of Coecke et al., (2010), integrating this model with conceptual spaces theory (Gärdenfors, 2014). A framework for understanding metaphor will be developed, and the model as a whole will be implemented within a cognitive architecture. Importantly, this architecture allows input from different senses, which is essential in dealing with analogy. Finally, the model will be implemented within a community of interacting agents. This model will be analysed to provide insight into how new concepts spread through a community of agents. This important phase will ensure that the system developed is able to learn novel ideas by interaction with other artificial intelligence (AI) systems and with humans. The impact of my research will be to improve human interaction with computers in everyday life. I am best placed to carry out this research because of my interest and background in human concept use, evolutionary and adaptive systems, and corpus semantics. The unique combination of expertise in formal semantics, computational semantics, quantum theory and category theory within the Institute of Logic, Language and Computation (ILLC) will complement my skills perfectly and ensure the success of this project.

title: Asymmetric Polyelectrolyte Multilayer Membranes for micro-pollutant removal
summary_nl:
There is growing awareness and concern about the presence of so called micro-pollutants (MP’s) in our surface water and drinking water. MP’s, very small organic molecules (100-1000 dalton) stem from industrial, medicinal and agricultural waste. They have the potential to cause long-term harm to humans and the environment, something especially true for MP’s classified as Endocrine Disrupting Chemicals for which it is known that even at very low concentrations they can have a significant negative effect on health and environment. 



Techniques to remove these MP’s from surface and drinking water are available but are currently too costly and/or inconvenient for the treatment of large streams of water. An example of this is the current state of art Reverse Osmosis (RO) treatment. RO membranes represent the densest membranes used in water treatment and have been found to successfully remove many MP’s. However, these membranes were designed with a very different application in mind (desalination) and have significant drawbacks. For proper operation at the high pressures needed for desalination, RO membranes have a thick active separation layer (> 100 nm) resulting in low permeabilities and thus a high energy demand for non-desalination applications. Furthermore, current RO membranes are very susceptible to fouling and to make matters worse, they have a low chemical stability against common cleaning methods employed in drinking water industry, e.g. chlorine treatment. This means that currently RO membranes can only be effectively used with an expensive pre-treatment to prevent membrane fouling. 



In this project we propose the development of a novel RO membrane specifically designed for the removal of MP’s. For this we turn to a very different chemistry: the self-assembly of oppositely charged polyelectrolytes at the interface of a porous support membrane. In this so-called Layer-by-Layer assembly, the support membrane is alternatively exposed to polycations and polyanions, to build polyelectrolyte multilayer’s (PEMs) of controllable thickness. A large advantage of this approach is that the properties of the PEM layer, responsible for the separation properties of the membrane, can be tuned by choice of polymer and by the employed coating conditions such as pH and ionic strength. This method thus allows the design of a membrane with optimal MP removal, by careful choice of the density, charge density and hydrophilicity of the PEM layer. Furthermore, we propose to coat these PEM membranes in a novel asymmetric fashion, where coating at a high ionic strength leads to the formation of a very open layer, 20-40 nm in thickness that prevents defect formation, after which coating at low ionic strength leads to an additional very thin (5-10 nm) and dense layer that performs the actual separation. This asymmetric approach to PEM multilayers is expected to provide very high selectivity (a very dense and defect free membrane) with very high water permeability due to the ultra-thin selective layer. Furthermore, PEM membranes are known to be much more resistant to chemical cleaning than current RO membranes. 



The versatility of this approach allows the PEMs to be grown on a multitude of substrates, thus allowing its use for the development of hollow fiber RO. In this membrane geometry the membrane is much less susceptible to fouling. In combination with its increased resistance to chemical cleaning these novel asymmetric PEM based RO membranes would allow for RO treatment without expensive pre-treatment.

title: ACEPOL: Aerosol Characterization from Polarimeter and Lidar
summary_nl: Aerosolen zijn kleine stofdeeltjes in de atmosfeer met een natuurlijke (zandstormen, oceaanzout) of menselijke oorsprong (fabrieken, uitlaatgassen van auto's). Aerosolen beïnvloeden het klimaat door zonlicht terug te kaatsen en de vorming van wolken te beïnvloeden en koelen daarmee de aarde af.  De grootte van dit afkoelend effect is niet goed bekend, en is daarmee een van de belangrijkste bronnen van onzekerheid bij het bepalen van de invloed van de mens op het klimaat. We hebben verschillende (combinaties van) instrumenten onderzocht om zo goed mogelijk de relevante eigenschappen van aerosolen te meten vanaf een satelliet.
summary_en:
Aerosols are small particles in the atmosphere with natural (sand storms, ocean salts) or anthropogenic (industry, cars) origin. Aerosols cool the climate by reflecting back solar light to space and by affecting the formation of clouds. The magnitude of this cooling effect is poorly known and represents the largest uncertainty for determining the effect of humans on the Earth's energy balance.

We have investigated different (combinations of) instruments to measure the relevant chraracteristics of aerosols from a satellite.

title: Space-based assessment of ozone deposition and its impact on ecosystem functioning
summary_nl: Het doel van de voorgestelde studie was om te beoordelen in hoeverre we satellietwaarnemingen konden gebruiken om de impact van luchtverontreiniging in de vorm van ozon op ecosysteemschaal fotosynthese te detecteren. De huidige schattingen van deze impact zijn voornamelijk gebaseerd op laboratoriumexperimenten. Als alternatief hebben we dit onderzocht door satellietwaarnemingen te combineren met een luchtkwaliteitsmodel op Europese schaal. Dit omvatte het gebruik van satellietwaarnemingen van gassen zoals stikstofdioxide die leiden tot de vorming van ozon. De studie toonde echter ook aan dat de kwaliteit van de huidige vegetatieproducten op ecosysteemschaal blijkbaar nog niet voldoende is om deze ozonimpact te detecteren.
summary_en: The main objective of the proposed study was to assess to what extent we could use satellite observations to detect the ecosystem-scale impact of the air pollutant ozone on plant photosynthesis. Current estimates of this impact are mainly based on laboratory experiments. Alternatively, we studied this by combining satellite observations with an European-scale air quality model. This included use of satellite observations of gases such as nitrogen dioxide that result in the formation of ozone. However, the study also revealed that apparently the quality of current ecosystem-scale vegetation products is not yet sufficient to allow detection of this ozone impact.

title: An unbiased metabolomics approach to understand how the undigested protein fraction in chickens and pigs impacts on gut health
summary_nl:
To overcome the gut health problems due to the undigested protein content in the large intestines of chickens and pigs in the animal industry, a better understanding of the interaction between feed utilization and animal health is required. Our project group is ideally suited to tackle this question, since we run a high-tech metabolomics facility with both untargeted and targeted metabolite platforms, with which we can establish the difference in metabolites in different parts of the intestinal lumen, blood, intestine and liver tissue as influenced by ileal undigested protein. In addition, the project group has ample know-how and experience investigating human gastrointestinal disease and murine models of gut inflammation, providing us with a solid background to investigate the mechanisms by which the metabolites may cause compromised gut health. The key objectives of our proposal are:

1.      To determine the changes in metabolites in intestinal content, blood, liver and intestinal tissue, and correlate these differences to changes in microbial species and gut epithelium determined by protein fermentation in chickens and pigs.

2.      To elucidate the mechanisms by which metabolites cause compromised gut health using organoids. 

3.      To validate whether interventions aiming at removing harmful metabolites/microbial species in the gut will increase gut health in mouse models of intestinal inflammation. This knowledge will be used to advice on changes in feed regimens for pigs and chickens to overcome the compromised gut health.

For the experiments in chickens and pigs, we collaborate with the Animal Nutrition Group (WUR) of Prof Wouter Hendriks, Dr. Walter Gerrits, and Dr. Rene Kwakkel (detailed in the respective applications). We offer to measure metabolites within our facility also for other members within the STW/DSM partnership, to study for example the effect of vitamins, fibre, protein source, and feed particle size on metabolite production. Together, our research will lead to a better understanding of how animal gut health is affected by feeding and food composition, and will potentially lead to new feeding regimens for chickens and pigs, improving animal health and decreasing the dependency on antibiotics.
summary_en: To overcome gut health problems due to protein fermentation in intestines of chickens and pigs in the animal industry, a better understanding of the interaction between feed utilization and animal health is required. The key objectives of our proposal are: i) to determine the changes in metabolites in intestinal content, and to correlate these changes to changes in microbial species and gut epithelium influenced by protein fermentation in chickens and pigs, ii) to elucidate the mechanisms by which these metabolites cause compromised gut health using organoid (mini-gut) technology and iii) to validate whether interventions aiming at removing harmful metabolites/gut bacteria will increase gut health. Together, our research will lead to a better understanding of how animal gut health is affected by feeding and food composition, and will lead to new recommendations for feeding regimens for chickens and pigs, that will improve animal health and decrease the dependency on antibiotics.

title:
Tm2+ based Luminescent Solar Concentrators:

Fundamental understanding and lab scale device.

(LumiCon)
funding_scheme: Open technologieprogramma OTP oud STW 2016 STW
summary_nl:
2.1    Research Summary 

Electricity generating glass is a holy grail in building-integrated photovoltaic’s (BIPV) as glass is omnipresent in our cities. Luminescent Solar Concentrator (LSC) technology can enable that by trapping part of the solar spectrum with a luminescent coating that guides solar energy to the perimeter by total internal reflection (like in a fibre optical cable) where solar cells convert it into electric power. Despite the large potential as PV-window, currently large area LSCs (>1 m2) only reach efficiencies of 1-3%, mainly due to the lack of suitable luminescent materials.

        Recently we discovered that cheap materials like NaCl and CaI2 doped with small quantities of divalent thulium (Tm2+) have high potential to establish 5-10 times higher LSC efficiencies. This is due to very special properties of Tm2+ that provide (i) 65% absorption of the solar spectral range (ii) no losses due to self-absorption and (iii) a potentially uniform absorption over the solar spectral range so that windows will remain colourless. 

        We aim to develop the first glass coating that can absorb the entire visible solar spectrum and transport the energy without self-absorption losses towards solar cells. For this we propose to first acquire fundamental understanding of how material composition and structure controls the 2+ valence stability of Tm. For the application the 1135nm 4f->4f emission of Tm2+ is required rather than the 5d->4f emission. Therefore, secondly we will study the various possible relaxation processes from the optically excited 5d states of Tm that eventually determines the quantum efficiency of the 4f->4f luminescence. Thirdly we will study the interaction of the Tm2+ 5d-states with the crystalline environment that ultimately determine solar absorption range. This knowledge will be used to select the best materials to be developed as coatings by sputtering.

        As effective research strategy we will use combinatorial co-sputtering to produce Tm2+ doped halide thin-films with a wide Tm concentration range and compound composition gradient. Our pilot version of Tm2+ doped films still shows too low efficiency and unwanted light scattering. We will therefore study the relation between parameters like sputter rate, substrate temperature, target composition and film properties like absorption, emission, light scattering and light transport, in order to gain understanding and control over the thin-film deposition process. 

 

        

2.2     Utilisation Summary 

        Our utilisation aim is to make a lab-scale LSC of 10x10cm2 with an anticipated power efficiency of 10%, 5 times more efficient than current LSCs, and a concentration factor of 10, which is a big step forward. It will be used to proof the high potential and applicability of Tm2+ based LSCs. As the efficiency of silicon solar cells is too low at the 1135nm emission wavelength of Tm2+, we will apply germanium and InGaAs solar cells in close collaboration with Fraunhofer ISE that is part of the user committee. 

        The utilization plan, set-up recently as part of our STW valorisation grant, is based on an analysis of the value chain and business case of a PV-window. Dutch companies of the value chain that are part of the user committee are Heijmans for the construction, UNStudio architects for the design and BASF as a chemical supplier. TUDelft already made a first step in the utilisation process with a spin-off company PowerWindow, headed by former LMR-group members, that is also part of the committee and will help to make the lab-scale LSC.

        The business case originates from a strong public and political desire to accelerate the integration of solar energy into the built environment and by the European Energy Performance of Buildings Directive, that requires “nearly zero-energy buildings” by 2020. In addition a LSC can benefit from BIPV being a major growth market especially in the building renovation sector. 

Furthermore PV-windows require no additional land-use and generate electricity where it is most needed without transport losses. They are cost-effective as windows are already present.

        If the above scientific challenges are met, it becomes possible to use a potential of 5000+ km2 glass building façade area in Europe alone for electricity-generation.
summary_en: In this project we will develop a cost-effective power-generating window based on the principle of a luminescent solar concentrator (LSC). This will be achieved with new luminescent materials doped with small quantities of Tm2+ that can absorb uniformly over the entire visible solar spectrum, re-emit and transport absorbed energy without self-absorption losses towards solar cells. The goal is to gain fundamental understanding of the valence stability of Tm2+, the relaxation processes within its excited 5d-states, gain control over the coating deposition process and make a record breaking 10x10cm2 LSC demonstrator.

title: Do I know what you know? Promoting students’ learning via accurate teacher judgments and adaptive support
summary_nl: Om hulp te kunnen geven die aansluit bij het niveau van leerlingen, is het nodig om kennis van leerlingen goed in te schatten. In dit project onderzochten wat hindert en helpt bij het maken van accurate inschattingen. Dit project liet zien dat docenten afgeleid worden door niet-relevante informatie (bv. de extraversie van een leerling). Het weghalen van niet-relevante informatie hielp niet; docenten verzonnen dan niet-relevante leerlingkenmerken. Verder hielp het wanneer de relevante informatie juist geïnterpreteerd werd. Digitale hulpmiddelen die inzicht geven in de kwaliteit van het werk van leerlingen (zgn. ‘learning analytics’) kunnen helpen bij het maken van betere inschattingen.
summary_en: To be able to provide support that is adapted to students’ needs, it is necessary to judge students’ understanding accurately. In this project, we investigated what hinders and what helps teachers in making accurate judgments. This project showed that teachers are distracted by irrelevant information (e.g., students’ extraversion). Removing the non-relevant information did not help; teachers fabricated non-relevant (student) information. Being able to interpret the relevant information well helped teachers’ judgments accuracy. Contemporary digital tools that provide insight into the quality of students’ work (i.e., learning analytics) can help teachers to make more accurate judgments.

title: Geographies of Food Consumption
summary_nl: The food-abundant environment is an important contributor to the obesity epidemic: it is all too easy to choose unhealthy foods. Yet, it is unclear how exactly the food environment affects food consumption. This lack of clarity is related to three current gaps in the research evidence. First, our understanding of people’s interaction with the food environment has been limited to single locations. However, the accumulation of all visited contexts in a day defines a person’s food environment. Also, non-food environmental characteristics should be integrated. Such characteristics may impact food consumption as a result of arousing stress, which, in turn, is associated with unhealthy food consumption. Second, there is hardly any insight in the effect of people’s allocation of multiple activities over different times and locations during the day (so-called ‘fragmentation’) on food consumption. I hypothesize fragmentation leads to increased stress levels during the day and as a consequence, will lead to an increase in unhealthy food consumption. Finally, it is unknown how knowledge and skills related to healthy food consumption (so-called food literacy) affect peoples’ responses upon the food environment. I propose that individuals with higher levels of food literacy are less vulnerable for the food-abundant environment. However, I expect that stress may temper its beneficial effects. Thereto, the overall aim of the proposed research is to determine interactions between the multiple-context (food) environment, fragmentation, food literacy and their impact on food consumption, including the assumed impact of stress. Building on important concepts from public health and human geography, a large field study will be conducted. I will use innovative, technology-driven methodologies for observation in naturalistic settings (i.e. smartphone application, wearable stress sensors). Hence, the study will provide novel and valuable public health insights by addressing critique moments in daily life, where and when individuals suffer from unhealthy food consumption.

title: Precision Ultrasonic Flow Meters using Matrix Transducers
funding_scheme: Partnership Bronkhorst-Krohne FLOW+ Real-time flow and composition measurement
summary_nl:
Ultrasonic flow meters are widely applied in a variety of applications. Compared to in-line meters, clamp-on meters, which employ a pair of transducers mounted on the pipe wall, are attractive as they can be installed without cutting the pipe. However, their stability is limited, and they are unable to measure flow profiles, which limits their linearity at low flow speeds. Moreover, their installation requires manual alignment of the transducers and input of a variety of setup parameters by the user. 

In this project, we will develop clamp-on meters based on matrix ultrasonic transducers to address these drawbacks. These transducers will consist of a two-dimensional array of 100+ elements and will enable beam steering in two directions, allowing us to develop three innovative measurement techniques: (1) automatic beam alignment by adjusting the steering angles so as to optimize the signal-to-noise ratio of the received pulse, thus simplifying installation and improving stability; (2) multi-path measurement by steering the beam at different angles, thus providing information about the flow profile; (3) self-calibration by using pulse-echo measurements between the elements of the matrix transducer to characterize the pipe wall and fluid, thus reducing the dependence on a-priori knowledge of their properties.

Building on our extensive expertise with matrix transducers and the associated electronics for medical applications, we will take three main original steps to realize these new clamp-on flow meters. (1) We will investigate the relevant wave-propagation phenomena, beamforming schemes and transducer design. Based on this, we will fabricate and characterize prototype matrix transducers. (2) We will develop integrated circuits with dedicated transmit and receive electronics to realize a cost-effective and accurate implementation of the beamforming and transit-time measurement. (3) We will combine these in flow-meter prototypes, in close collaboration with the users, to demonstrate our concepts in a realistic application context.
summary_en: Ultrasonic flow meters are widely applied in industry, and operate by measuring the flow-dependent transit time of an acoustic pulse through a fluid. To install such a meter, one can either cut the pipe carrying the fluid and insert a spool piece with built-in ultrasonic transducers, or clamp such transducers onto the pipe wall. The latter is much cheaper and more flexible, but comes with important disadvantages, such as alignment problems and poorer accuracy. In this project, we will develop a new class of clamp-on flow meters that employ so-called matrix transducers, which consist of many small acoustic transmitterreceivers that can be individually controlled by custom integrated electronics to steer the path of the acoustic pulses. This will enable several new measurement techniques, including automatic alignment and self-calibration, that will greatly improve the accuracy and applicability of clamp-on flow sensors.

title: Fair For All: Making Room for Fairness in the Globalised Economy
summary_nl:
Consider the following debate:



Sweatshop workers labour long hours at low wages, often earning less than 1% of the purchase price of the products they produce (Ross 2004). Wages in these sweatshops are criticised as unfair and exploitative (Snyder 2008) yet sweatshop defenders point out that wages are usually higher than available alternatives (Kristof 2009). 



The debate involves transactions ordinarily described as unfair (Vedantam 2015), but concerns about fairness are challenged because the actions nevertheless bring wellbeing benefits for individuals. This conflict between fairness and wellbeing has frustrated many similar debates. Progress requires:



(1) Some way to weigh both the values of fairness and wellbeing, 

(2) An account of what fairness is in these contexts, 

(3) Application of these insights to real-world cases.



My goal is to provide a moral theory that weighs fairness and wellbeing and, using this theory, to explain when transactions are fair. The resulting theory will be both ethically sound and compatible with the predominant paradigm in economics, neoclassical economics. Such a framework will allow for progress in social debates that have reached a stalemate. The project contains three parts. 



First, I will outline and defend an alternative to the moral theory of welfarism that is predominant in neoclassical economic theory. Welfarism claims that moral values depend only on individual wellbeing, leaving no room for fairness.



Second, I will develop an account of fair transaction that will explain what fairness is in economic contexts that employs the concept of power in bargaining situations.



Finally, I will apply the account of fairness to two cases: sweatshops and pharmaceutical prices. Although these are characteristic examples of conflicts between fairness and welfare, the project’s results apply in many similar contexts.

title: PiezoMEMS for FLOW+
funding_scheme: Partnership Bronkhorst-Krohne FLOW+ Real-time flow and composition measurement
summary_nl: In this project we will investigate the use of PZT piezoelectric layers in sensors for fluid flow, and fluid parameters like density and viscosity. We propose to combine PZT thin films with the so-called surface channel technology (SCT) that is used to realize silicon nitride tubes on a silicon chip. SCT technology has already shown to be a versatile technique that allows fabrication of a multitude of devices, e.g. thermal and Coriolis mass flow sensors, pressure sensors, micro valves, sensors for density, viscosity and thermal conductivity of the medium and sensors for IR spectroscopy. Adding piezoelectric actuation and detection will further enhance the possibilities offered by the technology.

We propose to combine PZT thin films with the so-called surface channel technology (SCT) that is used to realize silicon nitride tubes on a silicon chip. SCT technology has already shown to be a versatile technique that allows fabrication of a multitude of devices, e.g. thermal and Coriolis mass flow sensors, pressure sensors, micro valves, sensors for density, viscosity and thermal conductivity of the medium and sensors for IR spectroscopy. Adding piezoelectric actuation and detection will further enhance the possibilities offered by the technology.

title: Aan de slag met passend onderwijs: signaleren en passend begeleiden van (hoog)begaafde leerlingen in de klas
funding_scheme: NRO PPO Pilot werkplaatsen onderwijsonderzoek po
summary_nl:
Per 1 augustus 2014 is de wet Op Passend Onderwijs ingevoerd. Passend onderwijs houdt in: "Onderwijs dat leerlingen uitdaagt, dat uitgaat van hun mogelijkheden en rekening houdt met hun beperking" (www.passendonderwijs.nl/). In veel landen blijken leerkrachten onvoldoende tegemoet te komen aan de onderwijsbehoeften van (hoog)begaafde leerlingen, wat kan leiden tot minder motivatie en onderpresteren. (Hoog)begaafde leerlingen in Nederland presteren gemiddeld minder goed dan vergelijkbare leerlingen in andere landen. Met de invoering van passend onderwijs wordt ook van reguliere scholen verwacht dat zij betere begeleiding gaan bieden aan (hoog)begaafde leerlingen. Voor een betere aansluiting bij de specifieke onderwijsbehoeften van (hoog)begaafde leerlingen en om hen in staat te stellen zich optimaal te ontwikkelen, is het volgende nodig: (1) kennis van (hoog)begaafdheid en methodieken om (hoog)begaafde leerlingen zo vroeg mogelijk te signaleren en (2) passende strategieën om hen goed te kunnen begeleiden en motiveren zodat ze (blijven) presteren naar hun vermogens. In de beoogde werkplaats werken leerkrachten, pabodocenten en wetenschappers samen om de onderwijspraktijk voor (hoog)begaafde leerlingen te versterken. Doelstellingen van deze werkplaats zijn: 

(1) een duurzame professionele leergemeenschap vormgeven waarin samengewerkt wordt aan thema’s die aansluiten bij passend onderwijs. 

(2) kennisontwikkeling door wetenschappers, scholen en pabo aangaande signalering en passende begeleiding van jonge (hoog)begaafde leerlingen.

(3) kennis en methodieken aan leerkrachten (in opleiding) aanreiken, uitproberen en samen doorontwikkelen om (hoog)begaafde leerlingen te signaleren en passend te begeleiden.

Voor een betere aansluiting bij de specifieke onderwijsbehoeften van (hoog)begaafde leerlingen en om hen in staat te stellen zich optimaal te ontwikkelen, is het volgende nodig: (1) kennis van (hoog)begaafdheid en methodieken om (hoog)begaafde leerlingen zo vroeg mogelijk te signaleren en (2) passende strategieën om hen goed te kunnen begeleiden en motiveren zodat ze (blijven) presteren naar hun vermogens. In de beoogde werkplaats werken leerkrachten, pabodocenten en wetenschappers samen om de onderwijspraktijk voor (hoog)begaafde leerlingen te versterken. Doelstellingen van deze werkplaats zijn: 

(1) een duurzame professionele leergemeenschap vormgeven waarin samengewerkt wordt aan thema’s die aansluiten bij passend onderwijs. 

(2) kennisontwikkeling door wetenschappers, scholen en pabo aangaande signalering en passende begeleiding van jonge (hoog)begaafde leerlingen.

(3) kennis en methodieken aan leerkrachten (in opleiding) aanreiken, uitproberen en samen doorontwikkelen om (hoog)begaafde leerlingen te signaleren en passend te begeleiden.

title: Effects of individual and intergenerational life events on criminal behaviour: Disentangling environmental and genetic influences
summary_nl: De resultaten van dit project tonen dat criminaliteit sterk concentreert binnen families. Op basis van gegevens van tweelingen en van genetische risico-scores blijkt dat deze continuïteit van antisociaal gedrag tussen generaties voornamelijk het gevolg zijn van genetische invloeden. Dit toont dat het belangrijk is om te controleren voor genetische factoren wanneer oorzaken en gevolgen van criminaliteit onderzocht worden. Zo blijkt dat het verband van criminaliteit met individuele (zoals het hebben van een baan, partner of kinderen) en intergenerationele levensgebeurtenissen (zoals scheiding van ouders, een criminele vader of jong moederschap) overschat wordt wanneer niet gecontroleerd wordt voor genetische factoren.
summary_en: The results of this project show that crime is strongly concentrated within families. With data on twins and genetic risk-score it was shown that this intergenerational continuity of antisocial behavior is mainly caused by genetic influences. This indicates the importance of controlling for genetic factors when studying causes and consequence of criminal behavior are examined. Results show that the association of criminal behavior with individual (e.g., employment, marriage, parenthood) and intergenerational life events (e.g., parental divorce, paternal crime, early motherhood) are overestimated when genetic factors are not controlled for.

title: Model Learning for Sequential Decision Making
summary_nl: Reinforcement Learning is een tak binnen Kunstmatige Intelligentie die het leerproces van mensen modelleert maar de bekwaamheid waarmee mensen kunnen abstraheren en generaliseren is nog niet geëvenaard. In dit project hebben we bestudeerd hoe er gebruikgemaakt kan worden van het menselijke vermogen om effectief beslissingsproblemen te abstraheren en oplossingen voor onderdelen van het probleem te combineren. Door deze concepten in te bouwen in reinforcement learning hebben we algoritmes ontwikkeld die breder toepasbaar zijn.
summary_en: Reinforcement Learning is a branch of Artificial Intelligence that models the learning process of humans, but no computational agent has displayed the abstraction and generalization capabilities of humans. In this project, we studied how the human capabilities to effectively abstract decision problems and combine solutions to components of the overall problem can be leveraged. By embedding these tools into reinforcement learning, we developed algorithms that are more broadly applicable.

title: Nanostructured self-assembled functional materials
summary_nl: Materiaalonderzoek combineert wetenschappelijke bijdragen om geavanceerde functies te ontwikkelen. Nanoschaal manipulatie van materiaaleigenschappen maakt verbeterde functionaliteiten mogelijk, zoals waarneming, verwerking en zelfherstel. Zelfassemblage van nanocomponenten ontgrendelt nieuwe unieke eigenschappen en verbetert materiaalprecursors. Het doel was om zelfassemblage te gebruiken om nano-gestructureerde materialen op maat te maken. Het project omvatte universiteiten en industriële partners die diverse klassen van hiërarchisch gestructureerde vaste stoffen en dunne films ontwikkelden en onderzochten in het hele bereik van 2D tot 3D-materialen, met toepassingen in de auto-, staal-, halfgeleider- en fotovoltaïsche industrieën. Zelfgeassembleerde materialen kunnen bestaande materialen vervangen, prestaties verbeteren en implementatie in verschillende sectoren verbeteren.
summary_en: Materials research combines scientific contributions developing advanced functions. Nanoscale manipulation of material properties enables improved functionalities such as sensing, processing, and self-recovery. Self-assembly of nano-components unlocks new unique properties, enhancing material precursors. This proposal aimed to use self-assembly to tailor nanostructured materials, providing superior performance and added value compared to existing materials. The project involved universities and industrial partners developing diverse classes of hierarchically structured solids and thin-films, investigating the entire range from 2D to 3D materials, with applications in the automotive, steel, semiconductor, and photovoltaic industries. Self-assembled materials can replace existing materials, improve performance and deployment in various sectors.

title: Next UPPS - Integrated design methodology for Ultra Personalised Products and Services
summary_nl:
Products designed for mass-production do not match many people’s personal needs, often, an exact and personalised fit is essential. Emerging digital technologies like 3D scanners, cloud services, and advanced manufacturing enable true ‘mass personalisation’. At present, there is a lack of design methods for such personalised production; to combine emerging digital fabrication technologies to design.

Next UPPS sets out to develop an integrated design methodology for Ultra-Personalised Products and Services (UPPS), which will lead to valuable solutions for complex digital design workflows. In a unique interdisciplinary collaboration with the Dutch manufacturing industry and design studios, we will drive the transfer of knowledge and tools from the lab to production. This project encompasses three longitudinal case studies: sleep-enhancing respiration masks, protective workwear against hazards, and fitting shoes for safety and beyond. The end results of this project will ensure that Mass personalisation will become a new trend as easy-to-use design tools immediately involve end-users in the design practice.

title: Perfecting Metal Crystals
funding_scheme: Open technologieprogramma OTP oud STW 2016 STW
summary_nl:
We propose the development of a novel crystal growth apparatus that employs electromagnetic levitation to grow metal single crystals of a superior quality and purity under ultra-high vacuum conditions. During growth the metal crystals are not in contact with a container avoiding any stress induced effect arising from the contact between the walls of the container and the crystal.

Here, we propose to use electromagnetic levitation (EML) to grow superior quality elemental metal crystals that are not in contact with a crucible during growth and also do not experience the thermal gradients. The Lorentz forces that are mutually induced in a molten metal sphere by the radio frequency (RF) magnetic field from a coil can be used to compensate the force of gravity and prevent the thermal strain that results from mechanical contact between the melt and crystal. The challenges that we aim to address with this proposal reside not so much in the levitation process itself. In fact, it only takes a brief search on Youtube to find a multitude of movies that illustrate the idea at a hobbyist level. Instead, the reason EML has not been used to grow single crystals is that it is very difficult to create a stable enough environment that allows for the slow growth of an ideal single crystal that originates from a single nucleus. First, tiny deviations from a cylindrical geometry lead to an uncontrollable spinning motion of the molten metal sphere that prevents the controlled growth of a crystal. Second, the eddy currents that are induced for both levitation and heating of the metal sphere, also induce a fluid flow within the sphere that can be detrimental to the crystal quality

Within the context of this proposal two PhD projects are defined that will start off by each individually focusing on one of the two highlighted technical problems. Using finite element methods we will develop an optimal coil design and motion compensation mechanism, as well as model the resultant fluid flow. When the optimal design is converted into hardware we will characterize and apply the newly fabricated crystal spheres in both a physical and a chemical setting. One PhD student will focus on characterization of the purity and quality of crystals as well as the added value of these crystals as templates for the growth of novel two-dimensional materials such as silicene and germanene, whereas the second PhD student will explore the added value of these high quality and ultrapure single crystal for applications in the field of catalysis.

The quality and purity of the single crystals and their surfaces will be investigated with a broad arsenal of surface science techniques ranging from scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy, atomic force microscopy, Laue diffraction, low-energy electron microscopy, (micro) low-energy electron diffraction, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, Auger electron spectroscopy, and transmission electron microscopy to scanning electron microscopy.
summary_en: We will develop a novel crystal growth apparatus that employs electromagnetic levitation to grow metal single crystals of a superior quality and purity under ultra-high vacuum conditions. During growth the metal crystals are not in contact with a container avoiding and any stress induced effect arising from the contact between the walls of the container and the crystal. The purity and quality of the grown metal crystals will be carefully examined with a large arsenal of experimental techniques. We will also explore the added value of these high quality and ultrapure single crystal for applications in the fields of catalysis and the synthesis of novel two-dimensional materials.
